0.content:
Ameyalco Waters (also: Ameyalco): Ameyalco Waters is a coastal stretch of Natlan's Toyac Springs, in the land of the People of the Springs. It is a body of water formed where springs meet the coast, slightly warmer than the surrounding coastal waters, a warmth the official description attributes to magma chambers beneath. It is a place of surfing, Koholasaur riding and the Spiritway.

The name is Nahuatl, meaning "natural springs" or "at the spring". Toyac Springs, its parent area, is the home of the tribe that lives alongside the Koholasaurs and is known for hot springs and relaxing music.

Geography: Warm sea-and-spring water on the Natlan coast, with islands (one in the southeast starts a world quest) and an Underground Lava River that the story quests reach through a whirlpool. Its listed points include the Upper Sanctum and the Underground Lava River.

People: Residents named by the wiki are Anela, Aphila, Iwai, Pania and Rongo, plus the Master Trainers Avuia and Tepache, who are listed as "People of the Springs". A Koholasaurus also appears as an NPC.

Quests: The Tribal Chronicle "Journey to the Mysterious Island" (Where the Springs Return, Act III, version 5.0, Mualani's story) runs through the area: Someone Trustworthy, Where the Koholasaurs Gather, The Riddle of Sea and Sky and The Mysterious Island's Truth, the last entering a whirlpool into an underground cave. World quest "Stride on Rainbows, Split the Waves" (Rongo) and the daily commission "Swelling Springs" (a Spiritway sprint) are also here.

Status as of 7.1: Open and unchanged as of 7.1; no appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 story content was found.

1.content: Ameyalco Waters is the warm-water coast of Toyac Springs, in People of the Springs territory, where Koholasaurs are ridden along the Spiritway and Mualani guides outsiders.

2.content:
Ancestral Temple (also: Temple of Ancient Forebears): The Ancestral Temple is a sacred site on Coatepec Mountain in Natlan where people once communicated with the Night Kingdom. Today the tribes have a steadier link to the Night Kingdom, so the temple is unused, but it is still holy ground, guarded by the Scions of the Canopy.

Legba says only experienced Couriers who have passed three trials may enter. The in-game description evokes ancestors who made sacrifices here and prayed for a revelation that would change everything.

Geography: A subarea of Coatepec Mountain. Features include Nightsoul Totems, relay balls and ball path converters, and removable grappling hooks, so crossing it involves Nightsoul puzzles.

People: Legba, the Scions of the Canopy's contact, is the NPC placed here. The Scions of the Canopy keep guard.

Culture: Natlan's tribes treat the Night Kingdom as a realm tied to their dead and to Nightsoul. The temple is the older way in; the tribes later set up a more stable route. In the expedition text the land is described as one that did not belong entirely to humans, whose primitive elemental forces drained the soil's vitality.

History: Natlan's ancestors offered sacrifices here to their god and sought a revelation that would alter everything, according to the expedition description. When the tribes found a steadier connection to the Night Kingdom, the temple lost its practical role.

Travel: Entry is restricted to experienced Couriers who have passed three trials, per Legba.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple is disused but guarded, and remains holy ground.

3.content:
Ancient Mountain Path (also: Flowfire Experimentation Site): The Ancient Mountain Path is an old route on the volcano slopes of Atocpan in Natlan. It holds the Flowfire Experimentation Site, an ancient research station where dragon scholars worked out how to turn liquid Phlogiston into stone while the war against the powers of the heavens loomed. The station was abandoned long ago and is kept only by stone constructs.

It opens to the Traveler through a hidden exploration objective in Atocpan that begins by waking a giant stone serpent, a Secret Source Dragon Idol.

Geography: A subarea of Atocpan, on the lava-fed slopes of the Great Volcano of Tollan. The Flowfire Experimentation Site has a surface level and a deeper level, both reached by following the stone serpent into the cavern. A geothermal vent can be found among the exploration features here.

Places: The Flowfire Experimentation Site, with a surface area and a lower level. The records on the lower level are two golden-lit memory traces: an experimental report and a researcher's notes.

People: No living inhabitants are shown. The only presence is the unnamed researcher who wrote the notes, long gone, and the constructs left behind.

History: The experimental report records Experiment 150: the Type-01 Phlogiston Converter did turn liquid Phlogiston at the site into a solid. Extracting Phlogiston from it showed that the product was not solid Phlogiston but another sort of rock, the same stone formed when gaseous Phlogiston fuses with stone, as often happens in eruptions of the Tollan volcano. The researchers judged it interesting but not practical for their needs.

Dangers: The site is guarded by constructs set up as periodic defences. Lava, geothermal heat and Phlogiston currents are the other hazards.

Travel: Reached from Atocpan by completing the first step of the hidden exploration objective; a hidden teleport waypoint is unlocked inside.

Quests: How Long Must We Wait, My Friend? (an unofficial wiki name for a hidden exploration objective). The Traveler wakes the serpent, follows it into the cavern, runs the converter mechanism, and finally rides it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the site is still abandoned and open to exploration.

Nothing in canon through 7.1 says that the researcher returned.

4.comment: Ancient Mountain Path: Flowfire Experimentation Site
4.content: An ancient research station on the Ancient Mountain Path where dragon researchers tested a device that changed liquid Phlogiston into solid form. The first successful run produced a stone rather than solid Phlogiston, a result they put aside as impractical. The researchers intended to use a 'State Change' device to build fortifications from Phlogiston atop Tollan Volcano against attackers from beyond the sky. The writer of the notes left the site guarded by a Secret Source Servant and a Secret Source Dragon Idol.

key: Dragons' Residence in the Ancient Sacred Mountain
5.content:
Ancient Sacred Mountain (also: Sacred City of Tollan, Sacred City, Tollan, Land of Primal Flame, Dragons' Residence in the Ancient Sacred Mountain): The Ancient Sacred Mountain is the huge hollow inside the Great Volcano of Tollan in southwestern Natlan. It holds the Sacred City of Tollan, the capital of Natlantea, the dragon civilisation that ruled Natlan before human tribes. Its creator and master, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, was killed there when the human hero Xbalanque stormed the city, and Xbalanque died with him before being reborn as the first Pyro Archon. The city was then sealed for millennia and overrun by the Abyss. In 5.5 the Traveler, Paimon and the young saurian Little One leapt into the crater, restarted the city's machinery and reached its Heart. There Little One refused to activate Huitzilopochtli, a dragon device that would have burned all Natlan into phlogiston.

Today it is a terraced ruin lit by artificial suns (Astral Assemblages), crossed by rivers of liquid phlogiston and tended only by Secret Source machines. The map calls it the holy city of a proud nobility older than the tribes' woven-scroll histories, of which only a lonely tomb remains.

History: Xiuhcoatl was born from the primal flame on this mountain. He shaped the Sacred City there and moulded the Dragonborn from the primal flame. After the Heavenly Principles defeated the dragon sovereigns he lay in a false death while his brother Kukulkan ruled as Regent. When Nibelung returned, Xiuhcoatl woke corrupted by the Abyss. In his short spells of clarity he rebuilt the city and created the Astral Assemblages and Huitzilopochtli. Xbalanque's army later broke into Tollan, and he killed Xiuhcoatl by striking the eye that served as the array's control hub. The two Golden Entreaties that could start the array were split between Xbalanque and Kukulkan, and the city was sealed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Sacred City is an open but ruined area. It has been unsealed, much of the Abyss has been cleared, and Huitzilopochtli was not activated. Kukulkan faded away at the Heart, and Little One, freed of the Flamelord's Blessing, is a small Tepetlisaurus again.

This research found no 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 story content that returns here. Kukulkan warned that the city no longer had the energy to sustain the dragons living on as phlogiston and that they would perish without the primal flame's authority; once the maintenance functions failed, the wiki reads them as fading with him, though no scene shows it directly.

6.comment: Ancient Sacred Mountain: The finale in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain
6.content: In An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty (5.5), the Traveler and Little One offer the two Golden Entreaties in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain. A Source Dragon Mech traps the Traveler and Paimon. Guided by Kukulkan, Little One briefly takes a "mature dragon" form with the power of speech. Kukulkan reveals himself as the Sage of the Stolen Flame and shows him the Heart. He asks Little One to start Huitzilopochtli and rule a phlogiston world as a renewed Pyro Dragon Sovereign. Little One foresees an empty, eternal white world and cancels the array. He will not put the Traveler and Paimon at risk. He breaks back to them, the Mech is defeated and the Flamelord's Blessing is lifted. Kukulkan, alone by the array, admits he made the same choice long ago and fades. The volcano shakes, but only lets out a little smoke.

7.content: Huitzilopochtli, the "Sweeping Skyfire" or Natlan Phlogistonization Array, is the last great device of the ancient dragons. It stands in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain beneath the Great Volcano of Tollan. Kukulkan explained it to Little One. Xiuhcoatl built it to burn everything in Natlan and copy its information into phlogiston, turning the land into a realm of primal flame. Astral Assemblages would then destroy the Abyss on contact. Living things would either die or give up their bodies and become phlogiston lifeforms, and draconic ones would rule the new world. The array is started by the two Golden Entreaties, made from Xiuhcoatl's pupils, and needs three confirmations to activate or cancel. In 5.5 Little One cancelled it.

8.content: Astral Assemblages (Tzitzimimeh) are floating balls of phlogiston, pressed together into controllable miniature suns. Xiuhcoatl made the first at the Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds of the Sacred City, and the cold voice guiding the Traveler (taken to be Kukulkan) compared the feat to "lunar reconstruction". Their purpose is to fight the Abyss by mutual annihilation, but they cannot tell friend from foe. Three hang over the upper city and power the Celestial Axis. During The Frozen, Rekindling Land the Traveler stabilised the two that had been sealed or drained.

9.comment: Ancient Sacred Mountain: Chamber of Deliberation (Sacred City)
9.content: The Chamber of Deliberation is where the Thirteen Sovereign Lords of Natlantea met, with the First Lord as Speaker, to vote on government and judgment. Its records, written in phlogiston, survive. One is a vote to impeach Regent Kukulkan, with the Second Lord's argument erased and Kukulkan's mocking reply later surfacing over it. Another is a failed motion to burn down large human settlements. A third is the vote that condemned the Eighth Lord for her loyalty to her adopted human daughter Lianca. The Chamber still has working defences and a self-repair system. The Permit to the Sacred Heart was kept above it.

10.comment: Ancient Sacred Mountain: Secret Source Servants of Tollan
10.content: In the Sacred City, Secret Source Servants are dragon-made machines that still guard and maintain the ruins. A voice borrowed three of them to guide the Traveler and Little One, naming each after one of the fallen. Ehecatl was a servant a Qucusaur had stolen from the Tephric Ruins. Amaru was named after an arrogant lord who held the Celestial Axis to his death. Awanyu was named after a scribe of the Chamber of Deliberation. After the quest, Ehecatl's dormant body can be returned to the Tephric Ruins. A separate nameless prototype, built to help Xiuhcoatl record information, also speaks to them.

11.content:
Ancient Watchtower: The Ancient Watchtower is a domain in Natlan's Coatepec Mountain area, a ruin of enormous structures built long ago by the dragons of the land. Legend says those colossal beasts, having explored all the land and sea, raised these towers to look out toward the wider world beyond the sky. The dragons are long gone, and nobody today knows the true purpose of the place.

In-game it is a Forgery domain: clearing it yields weapon ascension materials. Its flavour text says the great dragon built many peculiar structures across the land and that old legends describe its outstretched wings blotting out the sky; the text wonders whether that was literal or a metaphor for the longing to see past the sky (the Sea of Stars). Only shattered remnants of the massive structures, and the patterns on them, let present-day people glimpse the forging techniques of that vanished civilisation.

Atmosphere: Vast broken masonry and pattern-marked fragments of giant structures under the Natlan sky; a silent monument to a people who looked upward and then disappeared.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is permanently accessible in Natlan. It carries no named plot; the dragons that built it are described as long vanished.

12.comment: Ancient Watchtower: Dragon builders of the Ancient Watchtower
12.content: The domain description attributes the watchtower-like structures to the ancient dragon civilisation of Natlan and says they were an attempt to see beyond the sky. This is flavour text from the domain; no quest explains the structures further, so treat the stated purpose as a legend ("Legend has it...") and not as confirmed history.

13.content:
Ashflow Street (also: The Unfinished Ashen City): Ashflow Street is a dead settlement at the foot of the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams in the ruined island of Ochkanatlan, Natlan. The in-game viewpoint calls it the Unfinished Ashen City: a place where people tried to found a new country on the ruins of a city built by a forgotten race, and where only ash remains. The alliance that gathered to build it has long since scattered.

It is a Version 5.2 location in the Ochkanatlan area. What a visitor finds are fragments: scrolls, recordings and a tower, left by priests, rangers, scholars and young mystics from different ages.

Geography: Ashflow Street sits at the base of the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams, the castle-like structure at the centre of Ochkanatlan. Vucub Caquix Tower stands in the middle of the street. The soundtrack Ashes of Presumption plays there.

Places: - **Vucub Caquix Tower:** a tower in the middle of the street, with a lower level reached by an elevator. Several scrolls and notes lie inside.
- **Cradle of Fleeting Dreams:** the castle-like structure above the street.
- **Recordkeeping Secret Source Sentinel:** an automaton used as a recorder, holding two recordings made very far apart in time.

History: The viewpoint text says the settlement was an attempt to found a new country on top of an older city built by a forgotten race, by an alliance that has since broken apart. The notes in the tower give a picture of its last days: a recording officer and a temple, craftspeople recruited to repair waterways, and a halt to the waterway work after a deep well was overrun by a dark calamity.

People: No living residents. The street holds the voices of the dead: the alliance-era priest and officials in the tower, and later visitors from the tribes. The visitors include a young Spiritcaller of the Masters of the Night-Wind (Liriwu), a mountain ranger and a traveling scholar, who came looking for the treasure rumoured to be aboard the Tonatiuh.

Atmosphere: Ash, stillness and the sense of an unfinished plan. Voices from earlier ages survive in notes and recordings, but nothing answers back. The mood is melancholy rather than action-heavy: people's last words and unkept promises.

Dangers: The ruins are described as cursed and Abyss-corrupted, and a dying adventurer's recording warns of monsters. A Spiritcaller's note reports that healing and mystic arts failed here. The same recording mentions the Flower-Feather Clan's blockade.

Travel: The settlement lies within forbidden Ochkanatlan. An elevator links the levels of Vucub Caquix Tower. The ranger's note says entering the city proper requires finding a mechanism that leads toward the sky-vessel, the Tonatiuh.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned and lifeless as of 7.1.

No source after 5.2 that was found revisits it.

14.comment: Ashflow Street: Vucub Caquix Tower Notes
14.content: Tower in the middle of Ashflow Street. Its scrolls and notes contain the ranger's account, the alliance-era priest's final record, a young Spiritcaller's diary and a scholar's analysis of an old scroll about a treasure on the Tonatiuh.

15.comment: Ashflow Street: Manqu and Sakkuk Recording
15.content: In Ashflow Street, a recording sentinel holds an old apology from Manqu to Sakkuk about an unkept promise and a feather accessory, and a much later dying adventurer's recording. A Manqu also appears in the tower's notes as the craftsman who replaced Chupicua on the waterway repair crew; the texts do not state outright that this is the same person.

16.content:
Atocpan: Atocpan is the volcanic southwest of Natlan. The Great Volcano of Tollan fills the region, an active volcano that erupts from time to time, and beside it lies the home of the Collective of Plenty (Teteocan), the tribe known for bodybuilding, wrestling and the best fruit and vegetables in Natlan. Ruins of the ancient dragons lie scattered around the slopes. The name Atocpan means "thick and fertile soil" in Nahuatl, which suits the rich volcanic farmland.

Atocpan is where Natlan's farming meets its oldest history: tribespeople grow crops beside a volcano that ancient legends call the Sacred Mountain, and the only way into the mountain's interior, the Ancient Sacred Mountain, is through the ring of floating islands above its mouth.

Geography: A region of ash-rich, fertile soil, orchards and rocky slopes around the Great Volcano of Tollan, in the southwest of Natlan. Its sub-areas are the Collective of Plenty settlement, Fallingstar Fields, the Remnants of Tetenanco, the Skyfire Circlet and the Ancient Mountain Path. The volcano encloses the whole region and periodically sends up fireballs.

Places: The Collective of Plenty settlement, with its Grand Wrestling Grounds (an elevated arena decorated with giant bull horns, also called the Resonating Arena) and training ground; Varesa's Orchard just outside the settlement; Fallingstar Fields with the Tephric Ruins; the Remnants of Tetenanco, ruins left by the ancient dragons; and the Skyfire Circlet, a ring of islands held above the volcano's mouth by Phlogiston.

People: The Collective of Plenty live here under their chief, Acatl. Their members include the playable Iansan, a champion wrestler, and the orchard-keeper Varesa. Their saurian companions are the charging Tatankasaurs. Mposo watches over the Tetenanco dig site.

History: Legend holds that ancient dragons once dwelt in the volcano and that their palace lay somewhere beneath the magma. According to the same legends, the dragon prince Kukulkan stole the primal fire (Phlogiston) from there. The first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, is said to have fought and defeated the dragon sovereign Xiuhcoatl on the volcano, after the Abyss corrupted him. After the dragon civilisation crumbled, the Abyss is said to have taken over the volcano.

Dangers: Volcanic eruptions (fireballs and rolling boulders, which are gameplay hazards in the game), saurians, Abyssal monsters and, near the ruins, Secret Source automata. Fatui camps are scattered through the area.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Atocpan is quiet, with its tribe prospering and the volcano still erupting now and then.

The Night Warden Wars ended in 5.3. The people of Natlan may now leave their homeland, and the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame has become a sports competition. Nothing in the later versions up to 7.1 changes the region's story.

17.comment: Atocpan: Collective of Plenty Settlement and Grand Wrestling Grounds
17.content: The Collective of Plenty settlement sits beside the Great Volcano of Tollan. Its centre is the Grand Wrestling Grounds, an elevated arena adorned with massive bull horns where the tribe's athletic competitions are held; a quest calls it the Resonating Arena. A bulletin board, referee, logistics manager and a flying squad member work here, and a training ground lies nearby.

18.comment: Atocpan: Remnants of Tetenanco and Fallingstar Fields
18.content: Two sets of ancient ruins. The Remnants of Tetenanco are the remains of what is believed to have been a dragon satellite city, destroyed in the war between the dragons and Xbalanque; today they are also called the Remnants of the Secret Source excavation site and are guarded by Mposo. Fallingstar Fields contains the Tephric Ruins, a section of ruins ejected from the volcano around five hundred years ago.

19.comment: Atocpan: Skyfire Circlet and Ancient Mountain Path
19.content: The Skyfire Circlet is a ring of islands suspended above the mouth of the Great Volcano of Tollan by the power of Phlogiston, and it contains the only entrance to the Ancient Sacred Mountain, hence its other name, Nahuatzin's Springboard. Secret Source Hunter-Seeker automata and sentinels are found there, and the Ancient Mountain Path leads up toward it.

20.content:
Basin of Unnumbered Flames: The Basin of Unnumbered Flames is the great bowl of land at the centre of Natlan. It holds the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, the nation's core landmark where the eternal Sacred Flame burns and the six tribes gather for the Pilgrimage, along with the fairgrounds and inns that serve it and the smoking Huitztli Hill to the north. Official text says the basin is not natural: something huge once crashed here, and no one knows what.

The Stadium is Natlan's main city and the seat of the Speaker's Chamber, so the basin is where tribal politics, tournaments and travellers meet. The surrounding land is dry and hot, with magma streams close beneath the surface.

Geography: A broad basin whose shape the Saurian Relics Association judged to be the scar of a colossal impact rather than a natural formation. The Stadium of the Sacred Flame sits within it; Huitztli Hill, a mountain the locals also call Smoke Ridge, rises to the north. Local specialty: brilliant chrysanthemum.

Places: The Stadium of the Sacred Flame, including three districts: Chuwen Fair (shops, food stalls and the Saurian Relics Association counter), the Temple of Pax, and the Warrior's Rest Area. Also the Weary Inn, the Speaker's Chamber, the Tablet of Tona and Huitztli Hill.

People: The Speaker's Chamber, the governing body of Natlan, sits in the Stadium. Tournament organisers, referees, engineers and warriors from all six tribes pass through the basin.

Culture: The Basin's identity is the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, a national combat tournament held at the Stadium. Official site text sums up the spirit of the place: in the name of victory and honour the fires of conflict are lit, and the fervour of all souls becomes fuel for the everlasting Sacred Flame.

History: Chapter V of the Archon Quest begins with a Pilgrimage held at the Stadium. After it, Kachina does not come back from the Night Warden War as the Ode of Resurrection should have restored her, and Mavuika suspends the Pilgrimage and the Wars while she investigates. The Archon Quest Echoes of Life, in the Black Stone Under a White Stone act, begins at the Speaker's Chamber.

Dangers: Wild saurians (yumkasaurs and tepetlisaurs), hilichurls, Forged Sand fighters and swiftstep couriers are the enemies listed for the hills, and Huitztli Hill is hot enough to trouble even tribespeople who handle Phlogiston. A boss, the Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant, lives there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the basin is at peace. The Stadium hosts the Pilgrimage as a sports competition.

The Sacred Flame was temporarily extinguished during the 5.1 invasion; the Abyss has since been purged from the Night Kingdom and the Stadium no longer sends warriors into war.

21.comment: Basin of Unnumbered Flames: Stadium of the Sacred Flame
21.content: The Stadium of the Sacred Flame is the core landmark of Natlan and the site of the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, in which members of the six tribes compete. A continually burning fire, the Sacred Flame, stands in it. The Stadium has three connected districts: Chuwen Fair, the Temple of Pax, and the Warrior's Rest Area.

22.comment: Basin of Unnumbered Flames: Huitztli Hill
22.content: A mountain north of the Stadium. Locals call it Smoke Ridge because magma streams from the Great Volcano of Tollan flow through it and send smoke up between its valleys. The heat is too much even for tribespeople used to Phlogiston, which may be why a reclusive Qucusaur lives there.

23.content:
Blazing Ruins: The Blazing Ruins are the remnants of a ring-shaped ceremonial site on Coatepec Mountain in Natlan, from an era before people truly mastered flame. Sages from all corners of the world came to ponder fire and tried to perfect the rituals needed to transform phlogiston. Today it is a domain overrun by scoundrels.

Several of the heroes who later followed the "mighty one" (Xbalanque, the Pyro Archon) into the belly of the volcano (the Ancient Sacred Mountain) are said to have trained here. The domain's description invites the player to cleanse the site and perhaps gain the revelations the ancients left. In gameplay terms it is a Mastery domain that yields talent level-up materials.

Status as of 7.1: Permanently available in Natlan as of 7.1; no plot events are tied to it.

24.comment: Blazing Ruins: Ceremonial ring of Coatepec Mountain
24.content: Ring-shaped ceremonial site where ancient sages practised and refined phlogiston-transforming rituals before flame was mastered; later a training place for some of Xbalanque's followers. Described by domain flavour text only.

25.content:
Bounama's Grocery: Bounama's Grocery is a small general-goods shop in the Chuwen Fair of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, in Natlan's Basin of Unnumbered Flames. It is run by Bounama, who is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind, and it sells ordinary cooking ingredients. The shop is open at all hours and restocks every day.

Bounama is protective of quiet: he asks customers to keep their voices down because noise can disturb the mixing process he carries out there. Payment is on trust. Customers take what they need and leave the money to one side, and a crafting bench in the shop may be used by anyone when it is free, without asking him first.

Places: The shop is a point of interest inside the Chuwen Fair, marked on the map as a general-goods vendor. It is not a separate district: it belongs to the fairground at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

People: Bounama is the only person associated with the shop. He is curt but willing to explain himself when someone asks a thoughtful question, and he is pleased by customers who think about environmental factors in crafting.

Economy: The stock is simple cooking ingredients, including mushrooms, salt, pepper, onions, milk, tomatoes, cabbage, potatoes, wheat and glabrous beans. Stock refreshes daily.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the shop is unchanged since its introduction in 5.0, and no later story role is recorded.

26.content: Bounama keeps Bounama's Grocery in the Chuwen Fair and is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind. He demands quiet because noise can disturb the mixing process, trusts customers to leave payment beside the goods, and lets anyone use the crafting bench when it is free. His only recorded idle line is a hushed "Shh!". No profile text, age or backstory is recorded.

27.content:
Brewblossom Stores: The Brewblossom Stores are an underground facility on Tete Isle, in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort off Natlan's western edge, where Aphimead is refined and stored. Visitors can take part in a hands-on brewing experience called Honeydew Craftbrew.

Aphimead is Tete Isle's specialty drink. It is made with the help of aphids that tend Brewblossoms, and the Stores are the place where that process is opened up to visitors as part of the resort's offering.

Places: The facility lies underground in the Northern Cavern of Tenochtzitoc, the older name of the resort island. It holds brewing barrels, a collecting device and refining equipment for Aphimead, plus storage for the finished mead.

Culture: Brewblossoms are plants known to possess spirits, and they close their petals on anyone who strays too close. Their pollen is a key ingredient of Aphimead. Brewblossom Aphids live with them in symbiosis, tending the flowers and feeding on nectar.

Quests: In the Story Quest The World Is Your Canvas! (the second part of the Sunspray Summer Resort), the Traveler's party is invited to try Honeydew Craftbrew. The staff member Takhar explains the process, and the bard Venti turns it into a friendly brewing competition with the Traveler. Venti jokes that the resort's meagre mead stock means visitors are meant to help replenish it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the facility is open as part of the resort. No role in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content is recorded.

28.content: Honeydew Craftbrew is the visitor experience in which guests steer Brewblossom Aphids to carry collected honeydew to the brewing equipment, raising brewing progress until a lever completes the batch. The wiki describes it as hosted at the Brewblossom Stores; in the quest Takhar frames it as a way to help produce the island's Aphimead.

29.content:
Castle Joquiratto: Castle Joquiratto is the stronghold of the villain "El Capoctus Joquiratto", the main antagonist of the immersive adventure experience at Villa Guiztli. It sits in the western zone of the Guiztli Ridge caverns in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. It is a comic, theatrical place full of scheming Nochtli lackeys, capybara and alpaca townsfolk, and booby-trapped chests.

Visitors play heroes defending the underground town from Joquiratto. The tone is pantomime: villains boast, barrels explode in the wrong direction, and treasure chests are rarely what they seem.

Geography: The castle lies in the Guiztli Ridge Inner Cavern, whose viewpoint is titled "Cavern of Stone and Prickly Pears". The resort island's older name, Tenochtzitoc, translates to "cavern of stone and prickly pears", though prickly pears no longer grow there in the modern day.

People: The area is occupied by Nochtli lackeys (the villain's henchmen) and by capybara and alpaca townsfolk, including an Alpaca Sheriff who speaks with a "meh" and leads the hunt for "the evil capybara". The lackeys shout "For El Capoctus Joquiratto!".

Quests: The Story Quest To Guiztli Ridge! (the Sunspray Summer Resort, part 2.2) has the party ride a cruise ship into the cavern, defeat bandits with the Sheriff, help activate a mechanism, and chase Joquiratto until his hot-air balloon is brought down and crashes on a mountaintop. The castle area is accessed partway through that quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the castle remains part of the resort and has no recorded role in later story content.

30.content: "El Capoctus Joquiratto" is the villain of Villa Guiztli's adventure show. His lackeys rob the town, the Sheriff asks the heroes for help, and in the Guiztli Ridge quest the party pursues him until his hot-air balloon is brought down. Nothing is recorded of any real person behind the title.

31.content:
Catastrophe's Edge: Catastrophe's Edge is an instanced trial area in Natlan's Tequemecan Valley. It lies beyond the Hall of Parting Vows and is entered through a portal during the world quest Revelations from the Past.

In that quest the Traveler and the Little One, a saurian companion, follow Manqu's guidance to the ruins to obtain a token left by the Sage of the Stolen Flame. After crossing a lava passage, a portal to Catastrophe's Edge appears, and the party must fight off three waves of foes there.

Quests: Revelations from the Past (5.0), part of the chapter Between Pledge and Forgettance, follows Rite of the Bold and precedes The Road Ahead. The Edge is the combat climax before the inscription and the token reward.

Travel: Unlocked through Revelations from the Past. Afterwards it can be re-entered by returning to the Hall of Parting Vows and going down the glowing stairs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the instance remains accessible from the Hall of Parting Vows. No later developments were found.

32.content:
Chamber of Deliberation: The Chamber of Deliberation is the assembly hall in the Sacred City of Tollan, inside Natlan's Ancient Sacred Mountain, where the Thirteen Sovereign Lords of the ancient dragon civilization once gathered to settle administrative and judicial matters. It is now a gold-trimmed, self-repairing ruin, and its preserved council records show a ruling class arguing over how to deal with humanity.

A "Speaker" presided and a numbered record was kept for each session. The surviving records show votes to impeach the Regent Kukulkan, to burn large human settlements, and to execute one of the lords for supposed betrayal. The hall also holds the permit needed to reach the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

Geography: Within the Ancient Sacred Mountain, the Chamber is a subarea on the dragons' level of the city. It has a second floor with a left passageway, a pool of lava, a dragon statue whose head hides one of the record boards, and a chamber of repair and purification facilities. The viewpoint here is named "Court of the Dragons".

Governance: The Thirteen Sovereign Lords were each styled by a title and numbered CL-01 to CL-13. CL-01, "Valiant One" Aj Nimalaj Chuq'ab Hun, acted as Speaker. Motions began with an agenda and were decided by vote; when consensus was reached, even those who abstained were bound by the decision. Any lord could bring a motion, and the Speaker invited the proposer to present the case before the vote.

History: The Chamber belonged to the era of the dragon civilization of Natlantea, whose capital was the Sacred City. The three readable records come from a time when the lords felt threatened by humanity's spread and its theft of the secrets of phlogiston.

Quests: Part of the World Quest Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment (inside In Search of a Hidden Heart, in the Chronicler of the Crumbling City series). The Traveler, with Paimon and the Little One, follows a Secret Source Servant that takes the name Awanyu, which once belonged to a scribe of the Chamber. A permit needed for the Heart of the Sacred Mountain was left above the Chamber, but Rifthounds have broken in and the permit receptacle is found empty. The party activates a purification device and the Chamber's self-repair, raises a phlogiston barrier, receives the permit receptacle and finally activates the Permit to the Sacred Heart.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Chamber is unchanged since 5.5: a ruined hall with its records open to the Traveler. No later story use is recorded.

33.comment: Chamber of Deliberation: Awanyu the Scribe's Servant
33.content: Awanyu is the name a Secret Source Servant takes in the quest, saying it once belonged to a scribe of the Chamber of Deliberation who seldom touched quill or ink himself once Secret Source Servants were invented. It guides the party to the Permit to the Sacred Heart while voicing its contempt for the hall.

34.content:
Chamber of Night's Trial (also: Trial Grounds of Restive Nightsouls): The Chamber of Night's Trial is a hidden arena in Natlan, in the Night Kingdom, resembling the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. It is entered by a visitor holding a Night Jade. A Nightsoul Spirit there invites the visitor to quiet the restless Nightsouls through battle.

Its in-game viewpoint is titled "Trial Grounds of Restive Nightsouls" and declares that only the blaze of battle can still these unquiet souls to slumber.

Geography: In the Basin of Unnumbered Flames, the entrance lies to the south of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. The chamber is a self-contained arena echoing the Stadium's layout rather than an open region.

People: The only inhabitant shown is the Nightsoul Spirit, a quest-only NPC who speaks in archaic, courtly phrasing. It says the Nightsouls here are like dreams of its mistress, the sleeping goddess of the night (Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night), and that when she wakes now and then they are single strains of her mind.

Dangers: The trial pits the visitor against eight Nightsoul warriors. Players have sixty seconds to defeat them all; success opens a set of reward chests and earns the achievement "By Battle Be Settled...". The challenge can be retried after failing (gameplay detail).

Travel: Access requires the Night Jade, a quest item formed automatically once three Shattered Night Jades are gathered. The shards come from the world quests "Revelations from the Past" and "To the Night, What is the Night's", and from a chest at the Phlogiston Extraction Research Center (a hidden exploration reward).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the chamber is still accessible as a permanent hidden challenge; no 6.x or 7.0-7.1 source found mentions it.

35.content:
Chamber of Weaving: The Chamber of Weaving is a minor point of interest within the Masters of the Night-Wind's Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land, in Natlan's Tezcatepetonco Range. Its only listed occupant is the NPC Yolotli, who is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind. Canon says very little about the place itself.

Yolotli explains that messages from Mr. Toltec often mean a new commission to investigate the Ley Lines, and that they are not ready to go out again yet.

Places: It is listed as a named point of interest inside the larger Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land, itself a ceremonial site of the Masters of the Night-Wind. The altar's other listed NPCs include the tribe's chief Biram, the High Priest Caholom, a guard named Cip, the Iktomisaurus elder Tlapo and Toltec.

People: Yolotli is the sole occupant. They sound anxious and apologetic, and consider many mystical arts and prepared materials necessary before travelling again. Their own Ley Line perception is mediocre, so they depend on Saurians for that task.

Culture: Yolotli is affiliated with the Masters of the Night-Wind and says there are many mystical arts to learn and materials to prepare first. In Yolotli's words, you cannot just choose any old mystical ability: it has to be the right one for you.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no change to the Chamber of Weaving is recorded, and it has no known role in later story content.

36.content: Yolotli is an open-world NPC in the Chamber of Weaving. They are nervous about a possible new Ley Line commission from Mr. Toltec, still preparing mystical arts and materials, and rely on Saurian help because their own Ley Line perception is only mediocre. They give the Traveler three Glowing Hornshrooms and a lesson in Iktomisaur etiquette. No further profile is recorded.

37.content:
Citlali's Home: Citlali's Home is the residence of Citlali, the great shaman of the Masters of the Night-Wind, in the Tezcatepetonco Range. It stands far from the tribal settlement and is hard to miss: its outer walls are covered in graffiti. Inside it is a mess of wine bottles, snacks and shelves crammed with light novels.

The Traveler first enters in The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors and gains permanent access after receiving Citlali's Handkerchief and Key in The Color of Memory. Citlali gave the key so that the Traveler wouldn't wake her by banging on the door while she was drunk.

Places: The home has an exterior, an interior instance, a bedroom, a table and a bookshelf. After The Color of Memory the bedroom door carries the faint sound of Citlali snoring, and the table and shelves hold books and the Traveler's note.

People: Only Citlali lives here. She has lived here as a recluse, reluctant to go out; Character Stories note that after she reached seventy she grew unwilling to leave her home and attended only to matters that demanded her involvement. For her birthday celebration, the tribe lured her out of her home with a knock at the door.

History: The home is the target of a Masters of the Night-Wind tradition: shamans have their students plaster its walls with taunts, as Huitzilin once did, so that Citlali becomes the formidable opponent who pushes them to improve.

Quests: In the Tribal Chronicles quest series Memories Flowing With Color, the interior is first accessed during The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors. In The Color of Memory the Traveler receives the handkerchief and key. If the Traveler has the limited-deluxe "Pretty Please, Kitsune Guuji?" and the first-edition "Shogun Almighty: Reborn as Raiden With Unlimited Power", they can be left on the table with a note from the Traveler and Paimon saying they were found while she slept.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Citlali's Home is unchanged: a permanent instanced interior, with no later story role recorded.

38.content: Among the Masters of the Night-Wind, a great shaman sometimes chooses a strong peer as an opponent for her students. Huitzilin chose Citlali and had students cover her home with taunting graffiti as a direct challenge. Citlali answered by humbling each arrogant novice. After Huitzilin's death, disciples continued the practice, claiming it was her dying wish. Most of the tribe accepted this, though it departed somewhat from tradition.

39.content:
Coatepec Mountain: Coatepec Mountain is a towering peak in Natlan and the home of the Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan), the tribe of explorers, couriers and hunters who live alongside the leaf-tongued Yumkasaurs. Their village hangs from the cliff-face, and the mountain is also the seat of the Turnfire rites in memory of the ancestor Yupanqui. The Pyro Archon Mavuika comes from this tribe. The name means "at the snake hill" in Nahuatl.

The terrain is harsh, but young people still come to test themselves. The mountain also holds the old Ancestral Temple, the lake at Teticpac Peak and, south of it, Firethief's Secret Isle.

Geography: A high, rocky mountain with the Scions of the Canopy's village suspended off the cliff-face. Official text says their ancestors hung giant trees over the cliffs with ropes and grappling hooks, which gave the tribe its name. Teticpac Peak is a plateau with a small lake at the very top; Firethief's Secret Isle lies in the sea to the south. Local specialty: quenepa berries.

Places: The tribal village; the Couriers' Longhouse; the Ancestral Temple; Teticpac Peak and the Manse of Monetoo Murals; Firethief's Secret Isle; and the Phlogiston Extraction Research Center.

People: The Scions of the Canopy, led by chief Wayna. They are skilled explorers, messengers and hunters, fond of extreme sports. The playable Kinich is one of their hunters, and the Pyro Archon Mavuika is of this tribe.

Culture: The tribe works as couriers and guides and honours its ancestors. Its great observance is Turnfire Night, held to commemorate Yupanqui, who is called the Firethief.

History: Tradition says that in the days of the tyrant Och-Kan, the tribe's ancestor Yupanqui stole the Turnfire, a fire that burned anyone who looked back at it, and turned it on Och-Kan's army. He glanced back and was consumed. He burned for a hundred days, and the fire pierced a hole through the Ley Lines so that he fell into the Night Kingdom, where the Turnfire is said to burn still. 'Malipo' became his Ancient Name.

Dangers: Steep terrain, wild saurians and the Fatui, who run a hidden facility on the mountain.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tribe is at peace and Kongamato's corruption is stabilised.

Natlan's war with the Abyss ended in 5.3, and the people of Natlan may now leave their homeland.

40.content: The Turnfire is a fire from the age of the Grand Alliance that tyrant Och-Kan used as a weapon; anyone it marked felt a terrible burning behind them and would be burned to a crisp if they turned around. Yupanqui stole it and used it against Och-Kan's army, but he looked back and burned. 'Malipo' is now an Ancient Name, borne by Burkina and by Kinich. The Scions of the Canopy hold Turnfire Night to honour their ancestors.

41.comment: Coatepec Mountain: Kongamato, the Mountain King
41.content: Kongamato is an enormous Yumkasaurus who has lived since the cataclysm and holds a special place in the Scions of the Canopy's heart. Abyssal corruption keeps him alive but also threatens to overwhelm him, so the tribe performs a ritual to drain it. After The Last Turnfire Night the corruption is stabilised, and he offers to train the tribe's young. The Archive text jokes that he is so large because he has lived so long and eaten too much.

42.content:
Colorfall Cave: Colorfall Cave lies just south of Colorfall Cliffs on the Easybreeze resort island. A crooked sideline used it as a hidden workshop for making fake Koholasaur dolls, and a young painter's apprentice named Zhaka was held there against his will until the Traveler freed him.

The shady arrangement belongs to Rekis, an underworld figure from Nod-Krai who is mentioned but never seen.

Geography: A cave south of Colorfall Cliffs, in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. Its map level is labelled as the eastern cavern of Tenochtzitoc, the island's old name.

People: Rekis's associates ran the workshop. Zhaka, Kanei's apprentice at the paint workshop, was taken there by mistake; his Asha companion is Azhka. After his rescue he appears at Easybreeze Market.

History: The cave was used for a counterfeit scheme during the resort's opening season. The scheme made fake Koholasaur dolls for tourists to buy, using a hostage painter.

Dangers: Rekis's henchmen were the threat while Zhaka was held. Nothing suggests that the cave is dangerous now.

Quests: Zhaka's rescue takes place here as part of the 5.8 Easybreeze content.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the workshop is abandoned and the cave is open.

Zhaka lives and works at the Easybreeze Market. Rekis's operations against Asha and tourists are not shown to continue.

43.content:
Colorfall Cliffs (also: Airborne Asha): Colorfall Cliffs are the sunny, colour-streaked fields of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. Above them hangs the resort's star attraction, the Airborne Asha, a floating structure shaped like an Asha holding a torch, which visitors ride a hot air balloon up to and paint.

The area has an Alpaca Park run by a manager named Aloha, and an attendant named Tikraq through whom the Airborne Asha can be revisited.

Geography: Wide green fields marked with vivid swirls of paint. Colorfall Cave lies just south, and Huha Hill's lodgings overlook the cliffs, along with Guiztli Ridge and Wavey Bay.

Places: The Airborne Asha, a giant floating structure resembling an Asha holding a torch, and the Alpaca Park.

People: Aloha, the Alpaca Park manager, and Tikraq.

Culture: The quest To Colorfall Cliffs! belongs to the 5.8 Sunspray Summer Resort event story, which asks the Traveler to colour the fields with Asha-powered paint drums.

Atmosphere: Bright colour, open sky and holiday cheer, with paint everywhere and tourists floating up to the sky attraction.

Dangers: Not hazardous; some Whopperflowers turn up during the paint-drum task in the quest.

Travel: Reached on foot from Easybreeze Market and Huha Hill. The Airborne Asha is reached by hot air balloon.

Quests: To Colorfall Cliffs! (part 2.1 of The World Is Your Canvas!) takes place here and at the Airborne Asha.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Colorfall Cliffs are open as a resort attraction.

44.content:
Concealed Land of Enigmas (also: Hidden Land of Enigmas, Enigmatic Land): The Concealed Land of Enigmas is a small cave hidden behind a waterfall west of Wavey Bay, in the Easybreeze Holiday Resort (also called Tenochtzitoc) on Natlan's western edge. A woven-scroll mystic arts implement at its end opens a portal to a temple that the wiki calls the Pyro Archon Temple. It is part of the quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc, added in 5.8.

The resort around it is a bright holiday area, but the cave is a quiet, forgotten place with something older behind it.

Geography: Behind the waterfall is a rock pile; breaking it reveals a short cave whose end holds the old implement, a woven scroll. The tourist beaches and attractions of Wavey Bay lie just east of it. Easybreeze Holiday Resort is a sparsely inhabited island off the westernmost edge of Natlan, and its Tenochtzitoc name is said by a local to mean a 'cavern of stone and prickly pears', though prickly pears no longer grow there.

History: Citlali reasons that the temple was built about five hundred years ago, by the Pyro Archons of that time, to temporarily contain Bakunawa, the Abyssal monster that devoured whole villages. The cave's implement was too old to work: its spirit had long dissipated, and Citlali said every caster is a different lock needing its own key. In the quest it was revived when the Asha, benevolent souls of the Mare Jivari, were drawn to the relic of Sanhaj that the Traveler and Citlali carried.

Quests: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc (World Quest, 5.8) leads here via Enjou's redrawn map. It is a prerequisite that A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night! be completed before it starts. After the quest, the player can return to touch the implement; the temple's central stone then leads to the Night Kingdom and the Mare Jivari.

Atmosphere: After the cheerful noise of the resort the cave is silent: water curtain, damp stone, and an old unsettling hush. On the far side of the portal the light is strange and the Wayob cannot be sensed.

Dangers: Little in the cave itself. Beyond the temple, in the Mare Jivari, the quest fights a fragment of Bakunawa, whose power Enjou says can corrupt even the passage of time.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cave and portal are open to visitors; the Pyro Archon Temple can be reached again at will. No new development in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

45.comment: Concealed Land of Enigmas: Pyro Archon Temple
45.content: The 'Pyro Archon Temple' is the wiki's unofficial name for the sealed temple behind the Concealed Land's portal. It contains seven stone seats honouring heroes, a waterfall with tablets at its back, and two side rooms with a wind-worn booklet and a notebook. According to Citlali it was built about five hundred years ago to contain Bakunawa, and the heroes' legacy 'awakens' it. Its central structure leads to the Night Kingdom and, from there, to the Mare Jivari.

46.content:
Core of Chu'ulel (also: Core of Chuulel, Chu'ulel Light Core, Bloodline's Control Hub, New Core of Chu'ulel): The Core of Chu'ulel is a cavern beneath the Vision Serpent's Sanctum in Ochkanatlan, the ruined dragon city of Natlan. Inside is the Chu'ulel Light Core, a glowing orb that pulses like a heart and once powered all of Ochkanatlan. Och-Kan built this core by enslaving his own draconic half, and sealed his mind inside it to fight alongside his people. By 7.1 it has been cleansed of Abyssal energy but is spent, leaving only a piece of Pyrophosphorite.

The name echoes the Tzotzil and Tzeltal Maya word 'ch'ulel', the soul or essence centred in the heart (a real-world etymology noted by the wiki). Its maker is the Sacred Lord Och-Kan, who in the present day takes the form of the dragonspirit Cocouik.

Geography: A cavern below the Vision Serpent's Sanctum, reached after the quest Adventure in the Land of Mists. The map divides it into a Secret Path, with a tower, and an Interior, with tents, pots of scrolls and a transparent barrier gate, around the Light Core. In the quest the Traveler purges Abyssal blight from the ruin, after which the core drops. An adventurer's notes say the Secret Source Automatons here, unlike those elsewhere, seem to understand speech.

History: When Och-Kan became king of Ochkanatlan he tried to make the dragon inside the Old Core of Chu'ulel power the city for him, since its mechanisms responded only to draconic energy. She refused, and he trapped the dragon in the Old Core. Writing in the Holy Sovereign's Notes, concluded that the only way to build a core that owed allegiance to humanity alone was to enslave the 'draconic' part of himself, so that it would stay imprisoned beneath human boots even if his human parts perished. The result was the new Core of Chu'ulel, which only he could command.

Quests: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm, Act II: Adventure in the Land of Mists leads to the Sanctum; Palace of the Vision Serpent is set in the Core (cleansing the Abyss, protecting the fallen core from waves of monsters, and finding Pyrophosphorite wrapped in a nameless adventurer's notes). In Moment of Awakening Och-Kan names the Core as the place Bona woke him from.

Atmosphere: The heartbeat-like pulse of the Light Core, Abyssal blight eating at the structure, and tents and pots of scrolls left behind. The notes sound like a ruler reasoning his way toward ever harsher measures to keep his people safe.

Dangers: Abyssal blight, Abyssal vortices and the Tenebrous Mimesis and Thundercraven Rifthound enemies that attack the fallen core; Secret Source Automatons, though one fights beside the Traveler once the core is protected.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Core is cleansed but dead: the Light Core lost its last vitality, and what remains is a piece of Pyrophosphorite. Cocouik later regained Och-Kan's body and spoke as him before dying.

Cocouik's reawakening as Och-Kan and his death in Moment of Awakening ended his hold on the city. No later development in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

47.content: Cocouik is the small, turquoise-green dragonspirit that travels with the Traveler in Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm. The adventurer's notes describe waking it in the Core of Chu'ulel with Pyrophosphorite. In Moment of Awakening the dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, Och-Kan's body, is defeated; Cocouik's mind rejoins it and speaks as Och-Kan, who dies soon afterwards.

48.content:
Cradle of Fleeting Dreams (also: Cradle of Dreams): The Cradle of Fleeting Dreams is the castle-like structure at the centre of Ochkanatlan, the ruined ancient city of Natlan. It stands over Ashflow Street, the settlement at its base, and has a throne at the top of a staircase.

It is a Point of Interest in the Ochkanatlan area, added with Version 5.2. The meaning of the in-game name is not explained in the sources read.

Places: Ashflow Street lies at the foot of the building. A staircase leads up to the throne, and at its foot stands a pot of scrolls holding a Spiritcaller's note. The Vision Serpent's Sanctum is listed as a Point of Interest under the Cradle.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and abandoned; open for exploration in Ochkanatlan as of 7.1.

49.content:
Derelict Masonry Dock: The Derelict Masonry Dock is an abandoned dragon-era facility hidden deep in the heart of the mountain at Atocpan, in the Remnants of Tetenanco area of Natlan. In its day, ash-gray mechanisms (Secret Source Automatons) driven by golden runes did the labour of flesh there, bringing grand designs to life above pools of flame. It is now a desolate shell.

The flavour text says the era ended when tyrannical outsiders (linked on the wiki to the Heavenly Principles) arrived, after which the once-powerful dragon race stagnated in submission. The only visitors left are mourners of that vanished age. The text also promises treasures for those who long to reach beyond the heavens (Celestia). In gameplay terms it is a Domain of Blessing that drops artifacts.

Atmosphere: A cavernous, half-ruined shipyard-like space of dead machinery, flickering firelight and the shadow of a once-grand design.

Status as of 7.1: Permanently accessible in Natlan as of 7.1; no plot is tied to it.

50.comment: Derelict Masonry Dock: Golden-rune automatons of the dock
50.content: Flavour text: golden runes (Iridescent Inscription) drove ash-gray Secret Source Automatons that replaced manual labour in the dragons' workshops above liquid phlogiston. Not elaborated by quests; keep it as atmosphere.

51.content:
Easybreeze Holiday Resort (also: Tenochtzitoc): Easybreeze Holiday Resort is a bright, sparsely inhabited island off the westernmost edge of Natlan. It is also called Tenochtzitoc, the old settlement where the war with the Abyss began and finally ended. The resort opened in 5.8 for a trial summer season: sandy beaches, a market, dance stages and playful Asha, colour-loving mascots that are secretly the souls of people lost in the Mare Jivari. Behind the fun lies the grave of the hero Tenoch and a temple built to hold back the Bakunawa.

Tenochtzitoc means 'cavern of stone and prickly pears' in the local tongue, though prickly pears no longer grow here. The resort is the first summer-themed map added permanently to the game.

Geography: An island west of Natlan. Its main areas are Colorfall Cliffs (green fields streaked with swirling colour and the 'Airborne Asha' attraction in the sky), Guiztli Ridge, Wavey Bay (sandy beaches, pristine water, water attractions) and Tete Isle, along with the Easybreeze Market and the Concealed Land of Enigmas.

Places: Easybreeze Market, the resort's commercial hub and many visitors' first stop, with restaurants, specialty shops and decor by the local Asha. Tete Isle, a lively island known for the specialty drink Aphimead, with a Dance-Off Stage, Brewblossom Stores, Me & Dew and The Dewdrop. Colorfall Cliffs, Wavey Bay and Guiztli Ridge, each with attractions. The Concealed Land of Enigmas and the Pyro Archon Temple.

People: Resort staff, vendors and tourists, together with Asha. The resort staff, many Natlanese, run lodging, food and attractions. Mualani, Chasca, Bennett, and other visitors tested the new resort in 5.8.

Culture: During the Sunspray Summer Resort event of 5.8 the resort's opening was marked with attractions and games, and the Natlan Adventurers' Guild sent invitations to adventurers across Teyvat to try the resort out.

History: Before the cataclysm the Muratan tribe settled at Tenochtzitoc. About five hundred years ago the Abyss invaded and the Bakunawa, a mountain-sized beast made by Rhinedottir, devoured villages on the west of Natlan. The hero Tenoch, a Muratan who had been exiled for his battle-mania, was the last survivor of the settlement. He gathered six allies from the tribes and led them into a battle against the Abyss at the place that became the Mare Jivari. Natlan/History marks the Abyss's invasion in that year as the start of the Night Warden Wars.

Dangers: The resort is mostly safe, though a few hilichurls turn up in quest areas and Abyssal monsters lurk in the caves tied to the Mare Jivari. Pirates from Nasha Town, led by Radius Bone Jack, are mentioned in letters on Tete Isle.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the resort is open. Venti and Mavuika have guided the souls who wished to return home out of the Mare Jivari.

Only a small corner of the Mare Jivari is explorable. The Bakunawa is restrained but could return.

52.content: Asha are exploration-mechanic Monetoo exclusive to the resort and its mascots. They roam freely, and some are created from the souls of those who perished in the Mare Jivari. They are more sociable and intelligent than ordinary Monetoo. Asha can also be created by human hands: the Masters of the Night-Wind priest Alu made the Asha Zolton while researching a link between Asha and Saurian Inscriptions.

53.comment: Easybreeze Holiday Resort: Pyro Archon Temple and the Bakunawa
53.content: The Pyro Archon Temple is reached from the Concealed Land of Enigmas. Citlali believes the Pyro Archons built it about five hundred years ago to contain the Bakunawa. It has stone tablets from several Pyro Archons and monuments for Tenoch and the heroes who fought with him.

54.content: Tenoch, also known by the title Tenoyollotzin, was a Muratan warrior exiled for his battle-mania yet respected by the other tribes. His giant obsidian club, the Talking Stick, got its name from his habit of using it to 'mediate' disputes. He gathered six heroes to resist the Abyss and died at the Mare Jivari with Sanhaj. He could not be revived by the Ode of Resurrection because he had already lost his Ancient Name.

55.content:
Easybreeze Market: Easybreeze Market is the commercial heart of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort and often the first place tourists see. It has restaurants, specialty shops and playful decor made by the resort's Asha.

Vendors here include the owners of Asha's Treasure Trove, Floral Whispers and Shoal's Haven, a dessert seller and a seller of 'suns'.

Geography: The market is the resort's retail district and the entrance to the island's other areas, with Colorfall Cliffs, Huha Hill and Tete Isle nearby.

Places: Shops and restaurants: Asha's Treasure Trove (owner Macuahuitl), Floral Whispers (Motolinia), Shoal's Haven (owner Teuciztli, with Lawaia as an employee), Puff-Up Pauldrons (Mazatl), Street Fighting Fontainian (Tzompantli) and a dessert stall run by Fournier.

People: A large cast of vendors, tourists and Asha. Other named residents include Challwa (Gift Egg Ambassador), Kanei, Zhaka and Zhaka's Asha Azhka, and the Ceremonial Greeter 'Teteltetl'.

Culture: Part of the market's story was part of the 5.8 Sunspray Summer Resort event; several quests start with the Traveler arriving here.

History: Opened with the resort during its trial season. Quest Traces of Chroma is set here and concerns the Asha Zolton, which the Masters of the Night-Wind priest Alu made.

Atmosphere: Busy, bright and relaxed: stalls and chatter, Asha weaving through the crowd and a feel of a holiday town.

Dangers: Safe. The only trouble linked to the market is the counterfeit Koholasaur doll scam, whose hostage worked in Colorfall Cave.

Quests: Traces of Chroma (world quest). To a Carefree Vacation! (resort story) begins with arrival and introductions.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the market is open.

56.content:
Esoteric Arrays: The Esoteric Arrays are a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, within the Great Volcano of Tollan in Natlan, where the ancient dragons once ran arrays that performed arithmetic calculations. Today the ruins are overgrown with Abyssal corrosion.

They lie on the way to the Heart of the Sacred Mountain. To uncover that path, the Traveler and the Little One must cleanse the corrupted ruins here, with the help of a Secret Source Servant and a Secret Source Beam Cannon.

Geography: The Arrays sit in the Dragons' Residence level of the Ancient Sacred Mountain. The ruins are ancient stonework, now fouled by Oozing Cores that carry the Abyss's corrosion.

People: No named residents. Secret Source Servants move through the ruins, and one is harassed by Rockfond Rifthound Whelps, and the Traveler defends it.

History: The arrays were built by the dragon civilization, which used them for arithmetic calculation. The wiki's source for this is the quest Where Once There Was a Calculation Array.

Quests: Where Once There Was a Calculation Array is one of three sub-quests in In Search of a Hidden Heart (part of the World Quest series Chronicler of the Crumbling City). The Traveler must clear Abyssal corrosion: defeat the Rockfond Rifthound Whelps accosting a Secret Source Servant, follow the Servant, defeat more whelps near the Dragon Idol, then use the Beam Cannon to destroy the Oozing Cores. The reward is a Phlogiston Unit.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Arrays are cleared of corrosion and idle; no later story role is recorded.

57.comment: Esoteric Arrays: Secret Source Beam Cannon
57.content: The Secret Source Dragon Idol at the Arrays unlocks the Secret Source Beam Cannon, a cannon that the Traveler fires to destroy the Abyssal Oozing Cores that foul the ruins. It receives a Lava Buff when the Traveler nears the exit.

58.content:
Fallingstar Fields (also: Tephric Ruins): Fallingstar Fields is a subarea of Atocpan in Natlan. It holds the Tephric Ruins, a section of old ruins that the volcano threw out about five hundred years ago, around the time of the cataclysm. Inside are broken pieces of Secret Source machinery arranged as if for worship, and a hidden room with a sealed report about the dragonborn.

The ruins are the setting of the world quest Investigator of Ancient Ruins and are connected to the old Secret Source Servant Ehecatl.

Geography: Open ground below the Great Volcano of Tollan with the Tephric Ruins at its centre. A local specialty is dracolite.

Places: The Tephric Ruins. Inside are a deactivated source core, three strange Secret Source structures and a floating ruins platform.

People: Nzaya and Kimosi are the tribespeople met during Investigator of Ancient Ruins, and the Traveler is joined by Little One.

History: The wiki says the ruins were thrown from the volcano roughly five hundred years ago, linking the date to the cataclysm.

Dangers: During Investigator of Ancient Ruins, Abyssal monsters and Hilichurls are in the ruins, and a mimic chest triggers an earthquake with falling stalactites while the Traveler fights.

Travel: Reached within Atocpan. The ruins can also be entered by dropping through a hole at the top.

Quests: Investigator of Ancient Ruins, which can stand in for A Brief History of Rocks to complete The Way Into the Mountain. The hidden room is tied to the story quest The Frozen, Rekindling Land, which yields the relic.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins stand quiet and open; the sealed report can be read.

No later change to the ruins is recorded through 7.1.

key: Items That Should Perhaps Be Deleted
59.content: The Tephric Ruins in Fallingstar Fields are a section of ancient ruins that the volcano ejected around five hundred years ago. They hold broken Secret Source Mechanism parts, an empty platform for the relic of the Secret Source Servant Ehecatl, and a hidden room whose sealed report discusses the regressed Dragonborn and the Flamelord's Blessing.

60.content:
Firethief's Secret Isle: Firethief's Secret Isle is a small island south of Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. It is hidden on the map and under constant cloud until all four of its time-trial challenges are completed. It was an ancient trial site and training ground, and only Saurians live there now.

The island is shaped a little like a dragon, and the wiki guesses it was named for the Dragon Prince who stole the flame of Phlogiston.

Geography: An island in the water south of Coatepec Mountain, with a central spot where the fourth challenge appears after the first three.

Places: Four time trial challenges: three that can be done in any order, and a fourth at the island's centre that appears afterwards. Unusually, none of them has a countdown timer.

People: Only Saurians live on the isle now.

History: The island was once an ancient trial site and training ground, presumably set up by Natlan's ancient dragons. Later humans seem to have repurposed it, judging by the buildings and graffiti.

Atmosphere: Before the challenges are cleared, a gloomy, cloud-covered island of old stone. After that it brightens.

Dangers: The challenges are puzzles, not combat; wild Saurians are the main living creatures.

Travel: Not on the map at first; the area is found by travelling south of Coatepec Mountain.

Quests: A set of four time trial challenges, with no storyline quest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the isle is a quiet training ground with only Saurian residents.

61.content:
Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds: The Flame-Melding Ritual Grounds are a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, in Natlan's Great Volcano of Tollan. According to the World Quest Sealed Site of Sacrifice it is where Xiuhcoatl created the first Astral Assemblage, a feat comparable to forging a star. The altar was sealed, and the Traveler unseals it.

Activating the Astral Assemblage replays a vision of the ritual: the dragons' success, a quarrel between its creator, identified as Xiuhcoatl, and Kukulkan, who addresses him as his king and elder brother, and a warning of a looming catastrophe. The place also holds the third "Iridescent Legacy" inscription, the last words of one of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords.

Geography: The site has an upper altar where the sealed Astral Assemblage stands, high above, and lower levels with pulverite and a furnace-shell mountain weasel guarding one inscription. The viewpoint here is called "Condensed Altar" and opens only after the quest.

History: The Ritual Grounds are where Xiuhcoatl created the first Astral Assemblage. Phlogiston was compressed under great pressure into a floating, controllable ball of heat, a miniature celestial body.

Quests: Sealed Site of Sacrifice is part of The Frozen, Rekindling Land (Chronicler of the Crumbling City). The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One find the Astral Assemblage locked high up, push stone platforms to form a path, break the seal and activate the device, triggering the vision.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grounds are unsealed and unchanged; no later story use is recorded.

62.content:
Furnace of Fiery Embers (also: Furnaces of Fiery Embers): The Furnace of Fiery Embers names five Source Mechanism sites in Ochkanatlan, Natlan: three in underground caverns (west, southwest and north) and two on small islands (east and southeast).

They are the focus of the hidden exploration objective Stoking the Ancient Flames (5.2). Each furnace has a matching Iridescent Inscription near an old sword, and the inscription reports whether the furnace has been rekindled.

Places: The wiki numbers the sites I to V, though the in-game map labels only some. Furnace I is reached by touching an Iridescent Inscription, II by entering a tower, and III after the achievement Clear the Area, Please! The eastern and southeastern furnaces sit on small islands and are not labelled with numbers.

Quests: Stoking the Ancient Flames is a quest-like exploration objective: activate all five furnaces, then draw the ancient sword. The first step grants the achievement Embers Rekindled and the second grants a copy of the Flute of Ezpitzal. These rewards are a gameplay detail.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the five furnaces remain sites to be rekindled by players. No later changes were found.

63.content:
Golden Dusk: Golden Dusk is a restaurant and lodge in the People of the Springs' settlement at Toyac Springs in Natlan, owned by Kupo Nui, the matriarch of the Nui family. It serves chilled drinks, has beautiful scenery and a convenient beach location, and has an in-house singer, Tirda.

It is an old Nui family home that was turned into a restaurant at Chief Amina's suggestion. Business is steady, but the family is frequently short-staffed. Guests may use the kitchen and sleep in tents near the water.

Places: A beachside house turned restaurant, with lodging and a bulletin board. The Hot Spring Retreat: Secret Menu furnishing is designed to resemble it.

People: Kupo Nui owns the place and greets visitors warmly; Mahina Nui staffs reception; Tirda sings; Wakea Nui appears at night.

History: Originally an old Nui family home, it was converted after Chief Amina noted the wonderful scenery and suggested a restaurant. It has been steadily busy ever since, with both locals and tourists enjoying drinks by the beach.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Golden Dusk remains open and steady, with no recorded story role after 5.0.

64.content: Inferno Stomach Supremo is a regional eating competition that has been held 242 times at Golden Dusk, according to its bulletin board. The current champion is Varesa of the Collective of Plenty.

65.content:
Grand Wrestling Grounds (also: Resonating Arena): The Grand Wrestling Grounds is an elevated arena decorated with massive bull horns in Atocpan, Natlan. It is the central hub of the Collective of Plenty tribe, where its many athletic competitions are held, and is also called the Resonating Arena.

Staff listed here include Macacoz, a professional wrestling referee, Muuziyaa of the Flying Squad and Tonaca, the logistics manager. Cuaxilo is also listed among the NPCs, and a Collective of Plenty Bulletin Board stands nearby.

Places: A raised arena crowned with bull horns, forming the central hub of the tribe in Atocpan.

People: Referees, runners and logistics staff of the Collective of Plenty work here. Their individual stories belong to their own entries.

Culture: Competition is a public pastime for the tribe: the arena hosts its many athletic contests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an active arena in Atocpan. No later changes were found.

66.content:
Great Volcano of Tollan (also: Volcano of Tollan, Sacred Mountain, Tollan Volcano): The Great Volcano of Tollan is the enormous active volcano that covers Atocpan in the southwest of Natlan. Ancient scrolls call it the Sacred Mountain. It still erupts from time to time and is said to have been far more active in darker ages. It was once the dwelling of the ancient dragons, and the legends of Natlan keep returning to it.

Legend says the dragons' palace lies beneath the magma, that the sage Kukulkan stole the primal fire from it in the form of Pyrophosphorite, and that Xbalanque fought and defeated the Abyss-corrupted Xiuhcoatl here. Inside the volcano lies the Ancient Sacred Mountain, an ancient city that the Traveler enters during the quest chain Path to the Flaming Peaks.

Geography: The volcano encompasses the whole of Atocpan in the southwest of Natlan, the same area that holds the home of the Collective of Plenty. The Skyfire Circlet crowns it, and the way into the mountain opens from there. The tribal legend of the Volcano Lord places a Shadow Pin above the Sulfurous Veins, a locale linked to the Children of Echoes.

Atmosphere: Heat, sulfur, ash and the rumble of a mountain that is never fully asleep. Eruptions rain burning rocks across the area and send boulders rolling in places, so people and creatures take cover until it passes and then carry on.

Dangers: The volcano erupts periodically. During an eruption fireballs of Pyro fall across Atocpan and hurt anything they hit, and enemies seek shelter too. Phlogiston inside the mountain is harmful to those who linger. In story terms, the pilgrimage to the volcano is deadly.

History: In ancient times the volcano was the dwelling of the Pyro dragons, and Xiuhcoatl shaped the city of Tollan inside it. When the dragon civilisation crumbled, the Abyss is said to have taken the mountain. Later, Xbalanque, not yet the Pyro Archon, fought and killed the corrupted Xiuhcoatl here.

Lore: Tradition says that bringing both Golden Entreaties to the volcano can wash the Flamelord's Blessing from a Saurian. The blessing is a mark tied to Xiuhcoatl that grows into uncontrollable power and madness. The tribes gave up the custom since no warrior ever succeeded, and now simply care for afflicted Saurians until they die.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the volcano is still active, still erupts, and remains an open-world landmark of Atocpan. Its interior can be entered after Nahuatzin's Leap. After the Traveler and Little One declined to activate Huitzilopochtli, the Tollan systems ceased maintenance and the draconic remnants faded; the array is obsolete.

Quests: Key quests: Nahuatzin's Leap (the first part of Path to the Flaming Peaks), where the party reaches the Skyfire Circlet and leaps into the crater, and An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty (the only part of A Finale Emberforged), set in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

67.comment: Great Volcano of Tollan: Xbalanque and Xiuhcoatl's battle
67.content: Long before the present, Xbalanque, not yet the Pyro Archon, fought the corrupted Xiuhcoatl at the volcano. He pierced the weak spots in the dragon's eyes, one of which split into two disc-like fragments, and both fell from a great height. Xiuhcoatl stayed dead while Xbalanque was wreathed in flame and revived. Whether anything of Xiuhcoatl remains is disputed.

68.comment: Great Volcano of Tollan: Golden Entreaties and the Flamelord's Blessing
68.content: The Golden Entreaties are two identical white discs with golden patterns, said to have been made from Xiuhcoatl's eyes. Legend claims that a strongly bonded human and Saurian can bring them to the volcano to cleanse the Saurian of the Flamelord's Blessing.

69.content: Huitzilopochtli is a device built by Xiuhcoatl in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain to turn Natlan into phlogiston and so destroy the Abyss, at the cost of nearly everything alive there. It is activated by reuniting the two Golden Entreaties.

70.comment: Great Volcano of Tollan: The Volcano Lord and the Shadow Pins
70.content: A tribal story told to Children of Echoes children. A giant black-and-purple salamander-like lord took the empty volcano, bathed in the springs, at its worst swallowed the Collective of Plenty, and finally coveted the gems of the Children of Echoes' valleys. Traore tricked it with a stone chamber, and the Wayob's four pins turned into phlogiston nails to pin it.

71.content:
Guiztli Path: Guiztli Path is a winding cavern linking Villa Guiztli to Castle Joquiratto on the Easybreeze resort island. It is a stretch of the resort's immersive adventure in which visitors play heroes defending a town from the villain El Capoctus Joquiratto.

Nochtli lackeys, the play-acting 'bandits', mill about the path in staged skirmishes.

Geography: A cavern under Guiztli Ridge. Villa Guiztli is the underground town at one end and Castle Joquiratto, the villain's stronghold, at the other.

People: Nochtli lackeys and the cardboard cutouts and Nochtlins of the villa.

Culture: The path belongs to a staged role-play adventure for tourists, not a real conflict.

Atmosphere: A theatrical cave: painted stage props, cheerful 'villains' and a sense of play.

Dangers: Mock ambushes; the chest in the exchange summons an Eroding Avatar of Lava, a gameplay challenge.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the path remains open as part of the attraction.

72.content:
Guiztli Ridge: Guiztli Ridge is a small island of the Easybreeze Holiday Resort, topped by a single rocky ridge. Beneath it lies Villa Guiztli, an underground town that offers a role-play adventure against a make-believe villain.

Its residents include a fruit farmer, a guard and a character named Achu.

Geography: A rock ridge on its own island. Visitors can see it from the Huha Hill lodgings. The caverns beneath hold Villa Guiztli, and Guiztli Path connects the villa to Castle Joquiratto.

People: "Achupalla", the Fruit Farmer, "Willapi", the Guard, and Achu.

Culture: Part of the 5.8 Sunspray Summer Resort story, in which a robbery in Villa Guiztli leads to a chase and a hunt for the culprits through the cavern, ending with the Traveler confronting the Nochtli ruffians.

History: Opened with the resort in 5.8.

Atmosphere: A rocky islet with a play-world below: quirky alpacas, capybaras and costumed villains.

Travel: The cavern below is entered from the ridge, and the quest has the Traveler ride a cruise ship through it.

Quests: To Guiztli Ridge! (part 2.2 of The World Is Your Canvas!).
