Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ridge remains open as part of the resort.

73.content:
Hall of Parting Vows (also: Sacred Path Trial Ruins): The Hall of Parting Vows is an underground ruin in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, said to be where Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon, and the Sage of the Stolen Flame swore a sacred oath. Players enter it during the world quest Revelations from the Past, seeking the token the Sage left.

Below it, glowing stairs lead down to Catastrophe's Edge, and an inscription there transports the player to the Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame. Its map has two levels, an entrance hall and the place of parting vows. A viewpoint inscription in the hall is titled Mural of Sworn Pledges.

Geography: Underground, with an entrance guarded by a barrier, corridors, a lava crossing and mechanisms. The ruin lies near the Children of Echoes in Tequemecan Valley.

History: Within the quest, Manqu explains from ancient tribal scrolls that the Sage believed humans could guide and lead Saurians to a better future than the age of the giant dragons. Feeling guilty for stealing phlogiston from dragonkind, the Sage hoped humans and Saurians could live as equals, and he left a token here; the scrolls say humans and Saurians each have their places.

Dangers: Abyss-corroded Rockfond Rifthounds guard the entrance, and a corroded Golden Wolflord appears in the final fight at Catastrophe's Edge.

Quests: Revelations from the Past (world quest, Tequemecan Valley, chapter 'Between Pledge and Forgettance'), played with Manqu, Paimon, the Traveler and the Little One Saurian; the player has the Traveler only for part of it.

Status as of 7.1: Completed ruin as of 7.1; can be revisited after the quest, with the lower sites reachable by the glowing stairs.

74.content:
Heart of Force Inversion: The Heart of Force Inversion is a subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, in Natlan's Great Volcano of Tollan, filled with pools of liquid phlogiston that flow upwards into the sky. Abyssal corrosion clogs its waterfalls until the Traveler clears it.

The World Quest Where Once Force Was Reversed sends the Traveler and the Little One here to destroy Oozing Cores and solidify the waterfalls with a Coagulation Pearl, opening the way toward the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

Geography: Liquid phlogiston cascades through channels and pools; one waterfall flows upwards towards the sky. Waterfalls of liquid phlogiston can be solidified into platforms and pillars, and corrosion has blocked some of the channels.

People: Secret Source Servants appear, and the Little One digs one out. Pyro Abyss Mages first accost the Servants, and Oozing Cores pelt the party with mud from above.

Quests: Where Once Force Was Reversed (World Quest, part of In Search of a Hidden Heart) can start by progressing In Search of a Hidden Heart or by defeating the Pyro Abyss Mages. The Traveler destroys the Oozing Cores and follows the Little One as the Servants turn waterfalls solid. At the top a new waterfall flows up from the pool's centre and is solidified into a tall pillar with the Coagulation Pearl, revealing a Phlogiston Unit.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the area has been cleansed and is unchanged; no later story use is recorded.

key: True Heart of the Sacred Mountain
75.content:
Heart of the Sacred Mountain (also: True Heart of the Sacred Mountain, Sacred Mountain's Heart): The Heart of the Sacred Mountain is the innermost chamber of the Great Volcano of Tollan, far below the ruined Sacred City in Natlan. It holds the heart of the primal flame (Phlogiston) and the last legacy of the ancient dragons: Huitzilopochtli, the Natlan Phlogistonization Array, a device made to burn Natlan into pure phlogiston and so destroy the Abyss. In 5.5 the Traveler and the saurian Little One reached it, and Little One chose not to run the machine. As of 7.1 it lies dormant and obsolete.

Entry requires both halves of the Golden Entreaty and a permit from the dragons' old records, and it is the destination of the Chronicler of the Crumbling City quest chapter. The Sage of the Stolen Flame, who stage-managed the journey, turns out to be the dragon Kukulkan.

Geography: The Heart lies under the Sacred City of Tollan, inside the volcano that dominates Atocpan. The way down is a fissure in the city centre that the dragon Xiuhcoatl excavated when he rebuilt the city, to give himself a stable place to experiment. A guardian Secret Source Dragon Idol seals the entrance and needs power from three Phlogiston Units. Inside, the story unfolds along a series of platforms, where Kukulkan recounts the history of the dragons, passes the dragons who gave up their bodies, and finally reaches the great array and its activation mechanism.

History: By Kukulkan's account, Xiuhcoatl was frozen in lava by the Heavenly Principles after their victory, and woke when the Dragon King Nibelung returned from beyond the sky. When the Heavenly Principles killed Nibelung, the Abyss-soaked Xiuhcoatl briefly regained clarity, saw how corrupted the world and his own mind had become, and spent his remaining lucid time building Huitzilopochtli. The device would turn Natlan into a land of only phlogiston, whose burning would be recorded and replicated, and the Abyss would be annihilated on contact. Kukulkan says every Dragonborn but himself accepted the plan; he walked away to look for another path.

Quests: The route is the two final parts of the Natlan wandering-saurian storyline. In Search of a Hidden Heart (Chronicler of the Crumbling City, part 2) sends the Traveler through the Sacred City: a nameless Secret Source Servant, a prototype built to help Xiuhcoatl keep records, explains that entry needs a permit from the Chamber of Deliberation and power for the guardian idol, obtained by clearing Abyssal corruption from several sites. An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty (A Finale Emberforged) is the ending.

Dangers: Abyssal corruption in the Sacred City above; the Secret Source Dragon Idol guardian; the Primeval Source Dragon Mech, with a laser cage and charged beam attacks; and the uncontrolled power of the Flamelord's Blessing if a saurian is unguided.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Heart is dormant. Huitzilopochtli has not been activated and is obsolete; Little One keeps a dimmed mark and has returned to his small saurian size.

The Flamelord's Blessing is gone. The volcano did not erupt in response, only releasing a little smoke. Kukulkan and the phlogistonised dragons faded away, and Tollan's maintenance functions ended. No later quest in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 returns here.

76.comment: Heart of the Sacred Mountain: Huitzilopochtli, the Natlan Phlogistonization Array
76.content: Huitzilopochtli, also called the Sunquake or Sweeping Skyfire, was the dragons' final weapon, kept in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain. It was built to turn all Natlan, and eventually the world, into phlogiston and matter made only of phlogiston. Everything burned would be transcribed and copied as phlogiston units, and the Abyss would be destroyed when astral assemblages from the primal flame attached to it. Dragons who gave up their bodies would become the rulers of the new world; ordinary life would die or be converted. It needs the two Golden Entreaties and three confirmations to start or stop.

77.comment: Heart of the Sacred Mountain: Golden Entreaties
77.content: The Golden Entreaties are two stone inscriptions that together form the control hub of Huitzilopochtli. They were created when Xbalanque and Kukulkan split the hub to guarantee the array would never run. One was kept by Och-Kan on the Tonatiuh (the legendary 'Jade of Return') and the other in the Hall of Parting Vows. Joined and offered in the Heart, they open the way to the array.

78.content:
Huha Hill: Huha Hill is the resort's lodging district: a cluster of villas and other places to stay, with rooftop pools, outdoor dining and a fine view of Colorfall Cliffs, Guiztli Ridge and Wavey Bay. A loading screen calls it a great area for tourists and says its name comes from the 'hooh... hah...' sounds often heard nearby.

Souvenirs from other resort areas decorate it once certain quests are done.

Geography: A hill above the resort looking over the cliffs, the ridge and the bay. Tete Isle is another part of the resort.

Places: Villas and lodging, rooftop pools and outdoor dining areas.

People: Tourists and resort staff.

Culture: Accommodation is expensive. According to Pumayna, some rooms cost 20,000 Mora per person per night, with fees for attractions elsewhere in the resort included.

Atmosphere: Comfortable and relaxed: an upmarket stay with views of the cliffs, the ridge and the bay.

Quests: Hosts reward decorations unlocked by the Sunspray Summer Resort story quests.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Huha Hill is open as the resort's lodging area.

79.content:
Huitztli Hill (also: Smoke Ridge): Huitztli Hill is a mountain north of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames. Local tribespeople call it Smoke Ridge because magma streams from the Great Volcano of Tollan run beneath it and send smoke up through its valleys. It is too hot even for people used to Phlogiston, which may be why a reclusive Qucusaur lives there.

Huitztli is a Nahuatl word meaning 'thorn' or 'spine'.

Geography: A mountainside with valleys that smoke. The base of the southern cliff face is strewn with the bones of a huge, unknown creature.

Places: Exploration features include a Coilgrass Sigil, an Everflame Seed, Flamegranate, Monetoo, Phlogiston Piles and Saurian Indwelling spots. A local specialty is brilliant chrysanthemum.

People: No settlement. The Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant is its notable resident.

Dangers: Extreme heat. Enemies are hilichurls, tepetlisauri, yumkasaurs and their whelps, Forged Sand fighters and Swiftstep couriers, plus the Goldflame Qucusaur Tyrant as the boss.

Travel: Found north of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the hill is still smoking wilderness.

80.content:
Isle of Tozoz (also: Isle of Night, The Isle of Night): The Isle of Tozoz, also called the Isle of Night, is a small island in the northeastern corner of Ochkanatlan in Natlan. It was once guarded by people who watched over saurian hatchlings and is now a quiet ruin of mechanisms and logs.

The world quest The Lone Isle Named Night (5.2) begins when the player activates three switches and the main Ancient Inscribed Ring. In a hidden chamber the Traveler and Paimon find a guard's diary and a Saurian egg, which the guard had named Aguara and which becomes a companion.

Geography: A small island at the northeast edge of Ochkanatlan, with switches placed high up, a summit the player climbs and a hidden underground chamber.

People: An unnamed guard kept the island under Lord Milchi. The diary also mentions Lord Atlatl and warriors from Cinder City who attacked the island.

History: Maintenance logs show a lax, low-budget watch: security was repeatedly judged too weak, but the approving party ruled that intruders should merely be driven off rather than harmed. A newer guard complained that the Saurians ate better than the staff, citing Lord Och-Kan's view that they were enemies.

Dangers: Secret Source Sentinels guard the island, and a Tenebrous Mimesis variant of an Iktomisaurus Warrior appears in the quest's combat step.

Quests: The Lone Isle Named Night belongs to the chapter In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons. Completing it unlocks an achievement and sends the Unhatched Saurian Egg to the Rest Area.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the island is abandoned, with Sentinels still active. No later developments were found.

81.comment: Isle of Tozoz: Isle of Tozoz Maintenance Logs
81.content: Logs and the diary on the island record a guard's complaints about budget, ladders and the lax care of the Saurians, as well as the officials' repeated order to avoid harming intruders. They are one guard's account and should be treated as partial.

82.content:
Land of Myriad Megaliths: The Land of Myriad Megaliths is a point of interest in the Sulfurous Veins area of Tequemecan Valley, Natlan. Its in-game viewpoint is titled Stone Chamber of Shifting Crystal Pillars.

The name and viewpoint title point to a stone chamber of crystal pillars. No lore, inhabitants or quest are documented for it in the sources read.

Geography: A chamber in the Sulfurous Veins section of Tequemecan Valley with its own map level.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an explorable location. No further information was found.

83.content:
Legendary Tonatiuh (also: Tonatiuh, Skyserpent Ship, Sky Serpent Ship, Legendary Skyserpent Ship): The Tonatiuh, also called the Skyserpent Ship, is a floating, dragon-built vessel high above the clouds over Ochkanatlan in Natlan. Legend made it Och-Kan's treasure ship, full of riches and containing a Jade of Return that could quell the Abyss, and adventurers chased it for generations. In fact it is a bleak, wind-scoured structure of islands and tangled lines, and the 'Jade' is a Golden Entreaty that Och-Kan hid there; Kukulkan invented the legend as a lure. As of 7.1 it is empty.

It is reached by placing Pyrophosphorite on the Altar of Primal Flame in Ochkanatlan, which raises a guiding wind. The ship is a spoiler-heavy location for the Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm quest chapter (5.2).

Geography: The Tonatiuh hangs above the sea of clouds over Ochkanatlan. From below it looks to Paimon like a vast ball of yarn or tangled snakes rather than a ship; on arrival it is a desolate scatter of floating islands and sand-covered structures, with Pyrophosphorite everywhere and an old mural on the north-western island. A mechanism like an Altar of Primal Flame stands on the ship; special flame-infused Pyrophosphorite ('Firestones') found around it activates the mechanism.

History: According to the wiki's reading of An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty, the dragons built the ship, originally to anchor the sky-cable ('stairway') that was to climb from Chichen Uctokah into space beyond Teyvat. Och-Kan, who took Ochkanatlan, turned it on its side and used it to hide a Golden Entreaty, one half of the control hub for Huitzilopochtli. Over the years countless adventurers from Natlan went looking for the ship, and none proved it existed. Bona's father Taika, with Copan, Titu and Legba, set out on the same search and never returned; the one survivor of that squad, a young mystic called Liriwu, came back from the city alone.

Quests: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm (Act II: A Dream of Gazing Upon the Distant Sky; Act III: The Tonatiuh Quivers). In To the Sky-Road, the Traveler, Paimon, Little One, Bona and Cocouik offer two chunks of Pyrophosphorite on the Altar and fly up. In The Other Side of the Sky they use Firestones to open a sealed rock and take out the 'Jade of Return', which turns out to be a Golden Entreaty; Bona becomes agitated and tries to warn them of a trap before the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash seizes it.

Atmosphere: Silence, wind and altitude: a lonely, sand-strewn structure among clouds, with the 'desolate' feel of a place that once held a mastermind's dream. A nameless adventurer's notes say it is nothing like they imagined, and that they could understand what the Python King felt at the end.

Dangers: Falling from the floating islands; the lingering trap, now destroyed; and, in the story, the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, which snatches the Entreaty from those who take it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Tonatiuh is empty and quiet. The trap set there by the Sage of the Stolen Flame has been destroyed, and the Golden Entreaty has been recovered by the Traveler.

The goggles left behind are the only testament to the adventurer who fought the maker of the trap, and an achievement awards the interaction. No later quest in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 returns here.

84.comment: Legendary Tonatiuh: The Jade of Return legend
84.content: The Jade of Return is said to be a treasure aboard the Tonatiuh that would 'cleanse filth' and quiet the Abyss in Natlan. Many adventurers, including Bona's father, died or vanished looking for it. It is a fiction: the object is the Golden Entreaty that Kukulkan tells the Traveler he made into a legend, calling it a trap for the 'lions of Natlan', and the inscriptions on it say it is hazardous and should not be touched.

85.content:
Leisurely Puffer: A watersports shop in Toyac Springs, in the People of the Springs' area of Natlan, owned by the family of the surfer Mualani.

It sells a wide range of gear, from swimsuits to waterskis, and its custom surfboards are said to be especially popular. A message board stands at the shop.

Places: The shop sits in the Toyac Springs area under the People of the Springs' name on the map. Its Leisurely Puffer Message Board is the shop's interactable.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

86.content:
Malinalco Grotto: Malinalco Grotto is an underground cavern in Quahuacan Cliff, Natlan. It contains a mural depicting the legend of Kuntur and Rumi, and is reached by taking the right-hand tunnel at the entrance of the Tenebrous Papilla boss cave.

Notes found there suggest the mural is being repaired by people who use paints produced on the spot. Two viewpoints are named Cavern of Tranquil Light and The Story Recorded. Hued Monetoo and Brilliant Chrysanthemum can be found in the cave.

Places: The cavern has several levels and the wiki names the area the Cavern of the Legendary Mural.

Culture: The notes treat creating murals near where paint is produced as a good idea, since missing colour can be refilled with material gathered on the spot.

Dangers: The tunnel lies beside the Tenebrous Papilla boss cave.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grotto remains accessible. No later developments were found.

87.comment: Malinalco Grotto: Kuntur and Rumi mural
87.content: The grotto's mural depicts the legend of Kuntur and Rumi, with Rumi called a wicked sorcerer in the restorers' notes. For the tale itself, see the item The Tale of Kuntur.

88.content:
Manse of Monetoo Murals: The Manse of Monetoo Murals is a point of interest on Teticpac Peak in Coatepec Mountain, Natlan. Its viewpoint is titled Where the Painted Realm Unfolds.

The name and viewpoint suggest a building with murals, but no inhabitants, history or quest are documented for it in the sources read.

Geography: Located on Teticpac Peak in the Coatepec Mountain area.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an explorable location. No further information was found.

89.content:
Mare Jivari (also: Silent Sea of Ashes, Ashen Sea): The Mare Jivari ('Silent Sea of Ashes') was a region at the far west of Tenochtzitoc in Natlan, once a sea of fire and now described as an endless plain of ash where the wind does not blow. It earned its name in a great battle of the cataclysm, when Tenoch and Sanhaj Kompore destroyed the Bakunawa there. Barbatos later blew it off the timeline, so it is cut off from the world.

Since version 5.8 a small corner is reachable through the Pyro Archon Temple, as a restricted story-mode area in which the Bakunawa can be fought. The rest is promised for later versions. As of 7.1 no further expansion is recorded on the pages read.

Geography: The westernmost part of Tenochtzitoc (now the Easybreeze Holiday Resort area). Loading text calls it an endless plain of ash where the wind does not blow. The playable portion is reached by touching the central structure in the Pyro Archon Temple and entering a portal in a Night Kingdom-like area, and is affected by Smoldering Ashes; it can be left only through the portal that appears when the Bakunawa is defeated, or by exiting the story mode.

People: No living inhabitants. Souls of people who died there, local Monetoo, and Abyssal monsters remain. Traces of earlier visitors include the Mondstadt adventurer Stanley and Tecpatl's Flintblades.

History: Legend says a phoenix lived in the sea of fire, worshipped as a totem and read by kings as a sign of nobility. A sage, the Lavawalker, made a circlet that could withstand the flames; his teacher and peers called this blasphemy and ordered him in, and he survived, wandering in and out for another hundred years until the fire burned him to ash. About a thousand years ago the Wanderer's Troupe came here while performing for foes, and its flautist met the Bakunawa, from which the troupe carved the Runestone.

Dangers: The Bakunawa, a huge permeated body with Anemo, Cryo and Geo attacks that ignores dash i-frames; Abyssal monsters in the simulated version; and smouldering ash. Many adventurers who tried to prove themselves here fell. After a defeat the Bakunawa is sealed only temporarily.

Quests: In the Sunspray Summer Resort event (limited-time) Mavuika and Barbatos (now Venti) open a rift between an Abyssal simulation of the Mare Jivari and the real one so that Venti can guide lost Mondstadter souls home; Bennett is targeted by the Abyss for escaping as an infant. In The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc the Traveler, Paimon and Citlali stop Enjou and enter the restricted real area, where they restrain the Bakunawa's permeation. Enjou then goes into the true Mare Jivari, which cannot be entered without the Bakunawa's power, looking for a forgotten homeland.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, a small area is open and the rest of the true Mare Jivari remains unexplored. Nahida calls it one of the places beyond her reach, implying Irminsul keeps no record of it.

90.content:
Mother Flamegranate Tree: The Mother Flamegranate Tree is a great tree in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, and the source of the Scions of the Canopy tribe's Flamegranates. Its roots, in a cave warmed by lava, grow the Mountain King Flamegranates.

Only Scions of the Canopy holding a special entry pass, the Green-Edged Paper Slip, may enter the root cave. Each pass bears its holder's name and cannot be traded. Tisoc has long served as guard at the cave entrance.

Geography: A tree on a cliff in Tequemecan Valley, with a cave of roots below. The roots have three map levels: a cool damp cave (before the quest), a warm cave (after it) and a geothermal surge.

People: Tisoc, the cave guard, calls himself an excellent one. The tribe guards the tree because it supplies its Flamegranates.

Culture: Flamegranate skins can be dried to make bags, such as those carried by couriers. Mountain King Flamegranates are an offering to Kongamato.

Quests: Ripe For Trouble (5.0): the Traveler and Paimon enter the cavern to find Tisoc, who has gone missing, explore the roots, break solidified magma and raise the Liquid Phlogiston levels, then flee before speaking to Tisoc again.

Dangers: Lava and solidified magma fill the root cave.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tree is ripe and still guarded by the Scions of the Canopy. No later changes were found.

91.content:
Muhuru's Gemporium: A gem shop in the Children of Echoes' settlement in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, run by Cheven.

Cheven's apprentice is Imix, and the NPC Iknal is also listed there. The shop sells gems and similar goods; the in-game vendor is Imix.

People: Cheven is the owner and Imix the apprentice. Iknal is listed at the shop without a stated role.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

92.content:
Natlan (also: Nation of War, Land of Saurians): Natlan is the nation of Pyro and of war in western Teyvat, beyond Sumeru's desert, a hot land of volcanoes, canyons, mesas and hot springs. Its people are the Natlanese, organised into six tribes, each bonded with one kind of Saurian, the evolved descendants of Natlan's ancient dragons. The Pyro Archon and God of War, currently Mavuika, is unlike other Archons: every Pyro Archon is a mortal human who won the throne through battle. For 500 years Natlan fought an unending war against the Abyss, until it was won in Archon Quest Chapter V.

Its heart is the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, where the ever-burning Sacred Flame stands; under Natlan lies the Night Kingdom, a realm of ancestral spirits (the Wayob) and the dead that serves as the nation's ley lines. Prized titles called Ancient Names, inherited through the generations, carry the deeds of past heroes.

Geography: Natlan lies west of the Great Red Sand, past the Desert of Hadramaveth. It is hot and volcanic, with canyons, mesas and hot springs. Each of the six tribes holds its own territory (Tequemecan Valley, Coatepec Mountain, Toyac Springs, Quahuacan Cliff, the Tezcatepetonco Range and Atocpan under the Great Volcano of Tollan) around the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames.

Government: The Pyro Archon leads Natlan from the Speaker's Chamber at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame; each tribe has its own chief.

By ancient tradition the six chiefs gather by the flame in the Speaker's Chamber at regular intervals and negotiate openly under the Archon's eye; the Chamber coordinates the Stadium's and the tribes' affairs and also appears to act as Natlan's highest court.

Religion: The tribes revere their ancestors and the Wayob: formless spirits, "will without form or thought", that dwell in the Night Kingdom, see past and future, protect their tribe and choose who receives Ancient Names. The dead go to the Night Kingdom, slowly merge into its sea of souls and are eventually reborn in Natlan in another form. Warriors draw power from these souls, the Nightsouls (Nightsoul's Blessing). The Sacred Flame, also called K'ahk', is the conduit to the Night Kingdom and the foundation of Natlan's defence.

Culture: The official description calls Natlan "the nation of oaths"; it prizes strength and competition, and "war" is part of everyday life. Visitors describe the Natlanese as energetic people whose "souls are forged for battle from birth", fond of graffiti, music, dancing and showing off. Warriors dress in imitation of their Saurian partners, whom people treat as family. Until the war ended, Natlanese could not safely leave the nation: outside its borders the Wayob's protection weakened and leavers suffered memory loss and emotional problems, so a chief had to seek the Wayob's approval before anyone departed.

History: Before humans ruled, Natlan was Natlantea, a dragon civilisation under Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, and the artificial Thirteen Sovereign Lords. About 2,000 years ago Xbalanque slew Xiuhcoatl and became the first Pyro Archon; the tribes then founded the Eternal Empire of Ochkanatlan under Kukulkan's half-dragon son Och-Kan, who became a tyrant until a scarlet-eyed youth, the second Pyro Archon, overthrew him. Five hundred years ago the Abyss struck Natlan harder than any other nation. The exiled warrior Tenoch and six heroes, one per tribe, fought beside the newly ascended Mavuika and drove it back, but it rooted itself in the Night Kingdom.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Natlan is at peace. The Abyss was purged from the Night Kingdom in 5.3 and the Night Warden Wars are over. Mavuika lives and still rules, because Capitano took her fated death upon himself. Natlanese may now leave the nation without harm, though they still need their chief's permission. Natlan no longer has its Pyro Gnosis.

Capitano merged with the Lord of the Night, making her undying so she can keep repairing the ley lines; his body sits dormant on the Throne of the Primal Fire atop Ochkanatlan. The Pilgrimage is now a sports competition. In 6.6 Mavuika gave the Pyro Gnosis away for good to help burn the corrupted Irminsul, and it vanished. The Archon Quest has moved to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII, 7.0-7.1). At its close, after Ronova destroyed a Celestial Nail in Snezhnaya with Eitr, the other Nails began emitting pillars of light, including the one near the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, right beside where people live. Mavuika, who blames the Heavenly Principles for most of Natlan's past disasters, is warning the population to watch for danger; what the phenomenon means is not yet known.

key: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame
93.comment: Natlan: The Pilgrimage and the Night Warden Wars
93.content: Every tribe fields warriors who fight alongside their Saurians, and the Flower-Feather Clan's Qucusaur Riders once patrolled all of Natlan. Until the war ended, the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame chose the strongest Ancient Name bearers to fight the Abyss in the Night Kingdom in the Night Warden Wars; fallen bearers could be revived by the Ode of Resurrection if at least one teammate came back victorious.

94.content: Six major tribes have existed since Och-Kan's era. Children of Echoes (Nanatzcayan, Tequemecan Valley): miners, excavators and gem appraisers, Geo, bonded with Tepetlisaurs. Scions of the Canopy (Huitztlan, Coatepec Mountain): couriers, hunters and explorers, Dendro, Yumkasaurs; Mavuika's birth tribe. People of the Springs (Meztli, Toyac Springs): guides and hot-spring keepers, Hydro, Koholasaurs. Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan, Quahuacan Cliff): rangers and riders, Pyro, Qucusaurs. Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan, Tezcatepetonco Range): shamans who monitor ley lines and Phlogiston, Cryo, Iktomisaurs. Collective of Plenty (Teteocan, Atocpan): farmers, bodybuilders and wrestlers, Electro, Tatankasaurs. Current chiefs: Pacal (Children of Echoes), Wayna (Scions), Amina (People of the Springs), Mutota (Flower-Feather), Biram (Night-Wind) and Acatl (Collective of Plenty).

95.content: Saurians are Natlan's dragons: Pyro vishaps that, after the Heavenly Principles cast down nails against Natlan's Phlogiston-rich soil, adapted by losing their intelligence (a "devolution" in the eyes of old dragons such as Kukulkan and Och-Kan). They now live closely with humans, choose their own partners and cannot speak human language, though tribe members read their moods. Phlogiston is an advanced form of Pyro, a programmable matter once used by the dragons, that powers Nightsoul's Blessing, Saurian abilities and Natlanese devices, and symbolises the people's indomitable spirit. Ancient dragon "Secret Source" machines still dot the land.

96.comment: Natlan: Ancient Names and the Heroes of Natlan
96.content: An Ancient Name (tocaitl) is a title embodying a virtue and an obsidian stone engraved with it, carrying the deeds of all its past bearers. The Wayob grant them to tribe members whose lives exemplify the Name; the Pyro Archon can also commission a new one, forged by a Name Engraver at the cost of part of their lifespan. Six Names belong to the Heroes of Natlan, first borne by Xbalanque's companions and then by Tenoch's six during the cataclysm. The modern heroes: Xilonen (Baraka), Kinich (Malipo), Mualani (Umoja), Chasca (Vuka), Ororon (Bidii) and Iansan (Uwezo). The Traveler is the first outlander to hold one, Tumaini, chosen by the Lord of the Night and forged by Xilonen.

97.content: In 5.0 Kachina fell in a victorious Night Warden War but the Ode of Resurrection failed to bring her back, because the Abyss had corrupted the Wayob. The Traveler, Mualani, Chasca and Iansan pulled her out of the Night Kingdom, and Mavuika burned the keepsakes her people had given her over the centuries, each holding Contending Fire, to rescue them. Mualani, then Ororon, then Chasca (after her adoptive sister Chuychu died of Abyssal contamination during a nationwide invasion) were acknowledged as heroes. With all six, Mavuika channelled Ronova's borrowed power to break the invasion. In 5.3 the Traveler, granted Pyro by the Lord of the Night, descended with Mavuika into the Night Kingdom, helped by the souls of the fallen, and destroyed Gosoythoth, the heart of the Abyss there, ending the war.

98.content: Mavuika kept the Pyro Gnosis only as a last resort, refusing to use it because rewriting the ley lines would erase Natlan's history; Capitano came for it but, after losing his duel with her, declined to take it while she was weakened and later abandoned his mission. During the 5.x invasion its power kept the Sacred Flame burning. In 6.6 Mavuika tossed it to the Traveler "to do with as you see fit", and Nahida used its flames to burn the corrupted Irminsul; the Gnosis then vanished. Mavuika sensed the loss and accepted it, saying this time there was to be no "returning", only giving.

99.content:
Natlantea (also: Natlantean civilization, Natlantean era): Natlantea was the civilisation that came before Natlan: an age when Pyro dragons ruled and humans lived in primitive tribes. Its lord was the Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl, served by the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, and its greatest city was the Sacred City of Tollan. The era ended when Xbalanque united an army, defeated Xiuhcoatl and became the first Pyro Archon.

Natlantea is not a place a traveller can visit as such; it is the ancient layer under today's Natlan. Its ruins, mechanisms and records are scattered across the nation, and the dragons of that age eventually devolved into the Saurians.

Geography: The land that is now Natlan, divided among the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, each of whom was given a territory to rule. Tollan was carved out by Xiuhcoatl himself and was said to be rivalled only by Chichen Uctokah. The wiki lists known sub-civilisations: Chichen Uctokah (the later Ochkanatlan, under the Lord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon), Ch'upikaq Tajin (now the Flower-Feather Clan's land, under Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak), Ek' Pulinik and Q'umqaraq'aj (unplaced), and the Tezcatepetonco Range (under Ix Kemonel Jasjatem Oox).

People: Xiuhcoatl, born from the Primal Flame as the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, and his younger brother Kukulkan, whom he made from a portion of that flame on the day of his own birth. The Thirteen Sovereign Lords were artificial intelligences made by Xiuhcoatl, regarded as his descendants and as the peak of Secret Source Mechanism technology. Below them stood the Three Princes. Humans lived in tribes under the dragons' brutal rule.

Governance: Rule by dragons over humans. Xiuhcoatl sat at the top; the Thirteen Sovereign Lords governed territories; councils of the Lords recorded debates, including over how to treat humans. Kukulkan served as Regent while Xiuhcoatl was incapacitated.

History: Xiuhcoatl was born from the Primal Flame and shaped the Pyro vishaps from it. The Heavenly Principles then arrived in Teyvat and defeated the Seven Sovereigns; Xiuhcoatl was frozen in lava and fell into a false death. Natlantea is thought to have come under Heavenly Principles control, overseen by Angels, with Kukulkan as Regent. When the Nibelung returned bearing the Abyss' power, its call woke Xiuhcoatl, who halted the Sovereign Lords' attempts to explore the stars and replicate moon-forging, retook control and devoured the Angels, an act that drove part of the unified civilisation into savagery.

Status as of 7.1: Natlantea is long gone. Its legacy survives as ruins, Secret Source machinery, the Great Volcano of Tollan and the Saurians, and the older layers of Natlan's history keep surfacing in the Archon Quests and world quests. Nothing newer than 7.1 changes this.

100.content: Before Xiuhcoatl could carry out his last plan, Xbalanque and the army he had united invaded Tollan, killing ten of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords and the Three Princes. He then fought Xiuhcoatl; as they fell from a great height Xbalanque came out of Xiuhcoatl's chest, reborn as the first Pyro Archon. His victory and a treaty with Kukulkan ended dragon rule.

key: Kingdom of the Lord of the Night
101.content:
Night Kingdom (also: Realm of the Wayob, Kingdom of the Lord of the Night, Land of Night): The Night Kingdom is a realm of souls deep beneath Natlan, described as "a liminal space between the body and mind, life and death". Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, built it from the fragments of Natlan's ancient ley lines, which were shattered in the war of funerary flame. Since then it has worked as Natlan's ley lines. The tribes' ancestral spirits, the Wayob, live there, and so do the souls of Natlan's dead. Natlanese warriors draw their "Nightsoul" power from those souls. For five hundred years after the cataclysm the Abyss occupied the realm. The Traveler and Mavuika purged it in 5.3.

The dead of Natlan go there and slowly lose themselves in a "sea of souls". In time they are reborn in Natlan in a different form. Ancient Name bearers who fell in the Night Warden Wars could be brought back out through the Ode of Resurrection, provided their team won. Because the realm is not like the ley lines elsewhere in Teyvat, it holds only memories made in Natlan, and for millennia it accepted only Natlanese souls.

History: In the war of funerary flame between the Descender and the dragons, Natlan's ley lines took the worst damage, and that opened a way for the Abyss. Guided by Ronova, the Lord of the Night rebuilt a similar network from what was left, and that network is the Night Kingdom. Xbalanque later strengthened it. In the cataclysm five hundred years ago, the Abyss was driven off the surface but rooted itself in the realm. That began the Night Warden Wars, which lasted five centuries and steadily wore the Wayob down. In 5.3 Mavuika and the Traveler destroyed Gosoythoth in its depths, and the Abyss was gone.

Travel: There is no road in. Known ways include the Pyro Archon stepping into the Sacred Flame during the Ode of Resurrection, and the Masters of the Night-Wind's rites (the Spiritspeaker Stone sent Kachina's rescuers). Capitano and Ororon also used a Masters' ritual to draw the Traveler's soul there. Obsidian totems scattered over Natlan act as contact points, and the Wayob can manifest on the surface through them and through Nightsouls.

Quests: Archon Quest Chapter V: Black Stone Under a White Stone (5.0, Into Eternal Night), Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors (5.1, To Whence the Smoke Drifts) and Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (5.3, the final descent). World quests include Peace to the Slumbering, The Mystery of Tecoloapan Beach and To the Night, What is the Night's. Act VI, A Space and Time for You (5.7), reveals what the Traveler's sibling did there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Night Kingdom is free of the Abyss and is being restored. The Lord of the Night is back inside it, maintaining Natlan's ley lines, and the Night Warden Wars are over.

Capitano gave his life in Mavuika's place and merged with the Lord of the Night. That made her undying and changed the realm's rules: the Night Kingdom now also takes in the souls of outlanders who die in Natlan, and Capitano led the souls he carried into it. Natlanese can now leave the country as often as they like, as long as their chief gives permission.

102.comment: Night Kingdom: Wayob Totems and Proxies
102.content: Mallko explained the realm's layout to Kachina's rescuers. Six main totem poles in the Night Kingdom are the "bodies" of the six tribes' Wayob, and countless proxy totems let each Wayob extend its awareness over the realm and track souls wherever they wander. A badly contaminated proxy can let a soul go missing. In 5.0 the rescuers cleansed one corrupted totem, and Mavuika said that otherwise that part of the realm would have been lost to the Abyss for good.

103.comment: Night Kingdom: Ode of Resurrection and the Night Kingdom
103.content: During the Ode, the Pyro Archon steps into the Sacred Flame and searches the Night Kingdom for the fallen warrior and their Ancient Name. If at least one of the warrior's team came back victorious, they could be brought back. A whole team that fell could not be. Souls left behind stay in the realm, and their Names are eventually lost. The Ode heals only the fatal wound. In 5.0 Mavuika came back without Kachina, finding neither her nor her Name, because the Abyss had cut the Wayob off.

104.comment: Night Kingdom: The Abyss in the Night Kingdom
104.content: After the cataclysm the Abyss took root in the Night Kingdom, and for five centuries Natlan sent its best Ancient Name bearers into the realm to fight it. The Wayob grew weaker and their tie to the tribes nearly broke. In 5.0 Mavuika judged that the realm would be lost in under a year. In 5.3, Mavuika and the Traveler descended to the deepest, most corrupted layer, where Gosoythoth, the "heart of the Abyss", had fled. It took the form of the fallen Pyro Dragon Xiuhcoatl, drawing on his memories in the ley lines, and taunted them in the voices of past Pyro Archons. They destroyed it, and the realm was purged.

105.comment: Night Kingdom: Capitano's Sacrifice and the New Rules
105.content: Mavuika had borrowed Ronova's power, and the price was her death. She meant to give her life to restore the Night Kingdom. The Lord of the Night waited for another who wished to take part: Capitano. He merged his existence with her, which turned his curse of undying life into her immortality and let him rewrite the realm's rules. Ronova withdrew her demand for Mavuika's death. Capitano led the souls he had carried, Khaenri'ahn and Natlanese alike, into the realm. From then on it also accepts outlanders who die in Natlan.

106.comment: Night Kingdom: The Sibling's Ley Line Weaving
106.content: The Traveler's sibling believed the Heavenly Principles had locked Teyvat's ley lines, but saw the Night Kingdom as an exception. After the war they had the Abyss Order fake an attack on Natlan's tribes to buy time. Meanwhile they entered the realm and negotiated with the Lord of the Night. Even the Night Kingdom could not host new ley lines, but she granted them room to run the Loom of Fate. Through it they wove the ley lines of New Khaenri'ah, which they now hold.

107.content:
Nursery of Nightmares: The Nursery of Nightmares is a space resembling the Night Kingdom in Ochkanatlan, Natlan. It is where the Traveler finished the chase for the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash in Moment of Awakening, where the dragon's corruption was purged and Och-Kan's soul was freed, and where Och-Kan's remains now lie.

The wiki lists it as a Point of Interest unlocked during the quest; the interactable remains describe him as the Python King, the Sacred Lord and the fell dragon, fully dragon and fully human, sleeping in silence until the end of time.

History: Cocouik's laser opens a gap in the fleeing dragon's defences, and the Traveler follows it into this space. A voice then introduces itself as Och-Kan, once ruler of Natlan, whose mind was infused into the city and whose soul had been devoured by the Abyss poison and turned into a furious dragon. The voice asks to be helped to purge the poison, and the dragon is defeated. Och-Kan speaks, now with his own mind, as the survivor of the Abyss's taint and as the one who in the past sealed his mind inside the Core of Chu'ulel.

Quests: Moment of Awakening, the second part of The Tonatiuh Quivers, in the Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm quest chapter (5.2). The steps are tracking the dragon, defeating it, speaking to the 'evil dragon', looking for answers in Och-Kan's memories, and collecting the Golden Entreaty.

Atmosphere: The place is dream-like and quiet; the quest's black-screen narration and golden text give it the feel of a recollection rather than a location.

Dangers: In the story, the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash fights with Golden Flame attacks. Nothing else hostile is listed.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Nursery is calm. Och-Kan's remains rest there; the dragon body and Cocouik's mind were reunited as Och-Kan, who died as the quest ended.

The Golden Entreaty found here was later joined with the other and used in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain (5.5). No development in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

108.content: After Moment of Awakening the Nursery contains Och-Kan's remains as an interactable. Its text calls him the Python King, the Sacred Lord and the fell dragon, fully dragon and fully human, who now slumbers in silence until the end of time.

109.content:
Ochkanatlan (also: Cinder City): Ochkanatlan, the Cinder City, is a ruined island city in Natlan, north of Quahuacan Cliff. It was built thousands of years ago by followers of Xbalanque on the remains of an older dragon city, and was ruled by the tyrant Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord, in the era of the Grand Alliance. Today it is thick with Abyssal corruption, shrouded in mist, and forbidden to the tribes. Any human found inside is either a memory of the past or a trespasser.

It is the setting of the world quest series Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm (Version 5.2), in which the Traveler follows a legend of a "Jade of Return" and learns that the legend was a lure laid by the dragon Kukulkan. At the end of that series Och-Kan's tainted body is put to rest and his mind, which the adventurer Bona had freed from the Core of Chu'ulel and named Cocouik, passes on.

Geography: A mist-covered island north of Quahuacan Cliff, with a castle-like structure, the Cradle of Fleeting Dreams, at its centre. Waterfalls and underground ruins lie below it. Above it, drifting over a sea of clouds, hangs the Tonatiuh.

Places: - **Cradle of Fleeting Dreams:** the castle-like structure at the island's centre, with a staircase up to a throne.
- **Vision Serpent's Sanctum:** the area above the Core of Chu'ulel, which lies in a cavern beneath it.
- **Core of Chu'ulel:** a cavern holding a glowing, heart-like light core that once powered all of Ochkanatlan. Abyssal corruption wore it down, and it loses its last vitality when cleansed.
- **Old Core of Chu'ulel:** underground chambers containing a huge dragon statue in which Och-Kan imprisoned the Dragonlord for millennia.

Atmosphere: Mist, ash and a constant sense of being watched. Waterfalls drown out the whispers that haunt former members of the adventure team. A scene here should feel like Natlan stripped of its festivals: quiet, ominous, and full of voices that should not be there.

Dangers: Abyssal corruption saturates the island. Expect Tenebrous Mimiflora, which imitate people (Quenin's double is one) to lure the unwary, hilichurls, Secret Source automata, Ruin Machines and the tainted dragon. Quenin claims people who stay near the ruins hear whimpering and see pale faces like their own.

Travel: Entry is forbidden by the tribes and the city is regarded as cursed. The Traveler goes in because of the Golden Entreaty seen in a vision at the Sage of the Stolen Flame's ruins, which points to Ochkanatlan.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Ochkanatlan is still a ruin and still officially forbidden, but the tainted dragon is gone.

The Core of Chu'ulel is spent, Ixlel is freed and the Tonatiuh's lure is exposed. The Golden Entreaty found there is now with the Traveler's party. No Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content that was found while researching this entry revisits the island.

110.content: Och-Kan, the Sacred Lord and Python King, was Kukulkan's son, a dragon with a human soul who revered Xbalanque; after Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame he took power and ruled the Cinder City as a tyrant. He was overthrown and split into a corrupted body (the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash) and a mind that lived on as the small spirit Cocouik. His full entry is historical.och-kan.

111.content: Legend held that the Tonatiuh, a ship drifting above the clouds, was full of treasure and of a weapon able to defeat the Abyss. Kukulkan invented the tale to lure brave adventurers for an experiment of his own. The Jade of Return is in fact a Golden Entreaty.

112.content: An unofficial name for the tribal adventurers who went to Ochkanatlan around the time of the Cataclysm in search of the Abyss-repelling treasure. Taika of the Flower-Feather Clan led them; only the young mystic Liriwu of the Masters of the Night-Wind came back alive.

113.comment: Ochkanatlan: Ixlel and the Old Core
113.content: The Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L, whom Paimon shortens to Ixlel, once ruled Chichen Uctokah. Och-Kan took her authority and sealed her in a statue in the Old Core of Chu'ulel, and she refused to power his city. In Open Your Heart to Me the Traveler frees her after millennia of torment.

114.content: The castle-like structure at the centre of Ochkanatlan, with a staircase up to a throne. A note left there by a Spiritcaller of the Masters of the Night-Wind records the horror of the creatures found nearby and a doubt about why the Python King died in the Abyss if he held a treasure that could destroy it.

115.content:
Old Core of Chu'ulel: The Old Core of Chu'ulel is a set of underground chambers beneath Ochkanatlan in Natlan. A giant dragon statue stands within, where Och-Kan trapped the Dragonlord Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L after seizing power in Ochkanatlan.

In the world quest Open Your Heart to Me (5.2), begun by placing the Ancient Flint Key in a small dragon statue, the Traveler and Paimon descend through the ruins and free the Dragonlord's soul from its imprisonment. It is a different place from the Core of Chu'ulel.

Geography: A multi-level descent: a winding road, a flooded work site with a waterfall, a hall of the ancient race and the mechanism heart around the statue. Abyssal energy blocks the entrance until the Traveler gains Cocouik's power.

People: Texts name Och-Kan with the titles Guardian of the Sacred Flame and Great Peacemaker, and mention the artisans Mahutzintl and Tlanalco and the workers Manqu and Sayani. Ixlel is a figure the Traveler meets in the quest.

History: Bulletins show forced labour under Och-Kan: rotating shifts of sixteen hours, extra grain for good teams, rations suspended for slow artisans, and deaths from falls and sickness. The texts frame the effort as being for the alliance against the dragons.

Dangers: Tenebrous Mimiflora, Secret Source Automaton hunter-seekers and Abyssal energy appear during the quest.

Quests: Open Your Heart to Me: reach the depths, deliver heart fragments to Ixlel, free her, evade a Secret Source Sentinel attack and take the Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon. Completing it unlocks the achievement Devoted to Eternal Serenity.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the chambers are open and the Dragonlord's soul has been freed. No later changes were found.

116.content:
Phlogiston Extraction Research Center (also: Extraction Research Center): A secret underground Fatui base inside Coatepec Mountain in Natlan. The Fatui extract Phlogiston there from captured Saurians, with machinery supplied by the Fontaine Research Institute.

It has two map levels, a passage and an experimental site, and a control room guarded by Fatui Skirmishers. Its documents show a bored, grumbling garrison rather than a fanatical one.

Geography: The base lies underground beneath Coatepec Mountain. Heavy extraction machinery runs on a core that can be shut down by a manual emergency brake, operated from two control consoles on either side, to prevent damage from malfunctions.

People: The garrison is Fatui. Each day two Fatui Skirmishers (Anemoboxer, Pyroslinger, Electrohammer, Geochanter or Cryogunner types) spawn in the control room. Notes name three soldiers: Vasily, Sidorenko and Nomokonov. The same three names make up the Polychrome Tri-Stars Local Legend, who are met far to the west at Huitztli Hill; the wiki links the names but does not explain the connection. Sidorenko appears to be the diarist who got locked in a cage and loses his Fire-Water to Vasily. Nomokonov is said to have had a technical background before joining the Fatui.

History: When the base was built is not stated. A diary says the soldier does not understand why such lengths are needed to capture Saurians from Natlan. Maintenance records show the Fontaine equipment in excellent condition, to the writer's surprise, who had expected cast-off gear.

Status as of 7.1: Active Fatui site as of 7.1; open to the player as a Point of Interest in Coatepec Mountain.

117.content:
Pseudostar Pedestal: A subarea in the Dragons' Residence of the Ancient Sacred Mountain (the Sacred City of Tollan) in Natlan, next to a teleport waypoint.

Its notable feature is a Secret Source Dragon Idol Workshop Engraving, a first-person declaration that the wiki attributes to Xiuhcoatl.

Places: Part of the Dragons' Residence map level. The engraving sits beside the Teleport Waypoint.

History: The engraving's speaker calls himself the Creator, Shaper and Forger of all names, and promises ruin on the enemies of Tollan, wishing disease and a collapse by the wayside on them. He says he will not be trampled by the usurper of the sky nor consumed by the black tides of the earth, and ties Tollan's glory and the radiance of the primal flame to the survival of his craft.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible as of 7.1, the same as the rest of the Ancient Sacred Mountain.

118.content:
Pyro Archon Temple: The Pyro Archon Temple is a hidden temple under the Easybreeze Holiday Resort area of Natlan, first entered in the quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc (5.8). Citlali guesses it was built about five hundred years ago by Pyro Archons to hold the Bakunawa. Its central stone structure opens onto the Night Kingdom and the Mare Jivari.

'Pyro Archon Temple' is an unofficial name used by the community wiki. It is an instance, reached again later through a mystic arts implement in the Concealed Land of Enigmas, a cave behind the waterfall west of Wavey Bay.

Geography: Beneath the Tenochtzitoc area. A central stone structure sits in the main hall; seven memorial stones stand behind it, five tablets are set near a waterfall at the back, and two side rooms hold a table each. Touching the central structure moves the player into a Night Kingdom-like space, whose portal leads to the Mare Jivari.

Places: The memorial stones carry short inscriptions, each for a hero of the old coalition: Tupac the giant, Menilek the brave, Sundjatta chief of the mines, Tenoch the everlasting (his remains are buried here), Wanjiru the great runner, Sanhaj Kompore the Border Master (his remains are buried here) and young Burkina.

History: Citlali's hypothesis is that the temple was raised five hundred years ago by Pyro Archons to temporarily contain the Bakunawa, a calamity left from the Natlan cataclysm. The inscriptions suggest several generations of guardians kept the seal and hid the place.

Dangers: The Bakunawa, a vast permeated body, can be fought from the Mare Jivari side; after defeat it is only sealed for a time.

Travel: Enter the Concealed Land of Enigmas, activate the mystic arts implement, then touch the central stone structure to enter the Night Kingdom-like area and the portal to the Mare Jivari.

Status as of 7.1: Open to visitors in the instance as of 7.1. The Bakunawa stays sealed between fights, and the wider Mare Jivari has not been opened beyond the 5.8 area.

119.content:
Quahuacan Cliff: Quahuacan Cliff is the cliff-top home of the Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan), the Natlan tribe that rides Qucusaurs, the flying saurians. The clan's riders once patrolled all of Natlan and still watch the ruins of Ochkanatlan. Since 5.8 the cliff also serves as the landing for people leaving Nod-Krai. The name may echo the Nahuatl Cuauhhuacan, a place name built from the words for tree and eagle.

It is a place of flight, pride and second chances: riders train here, the 'Wingless' who fail the rider exam find other work, and the clan's territory holds an old, long-sealed Secret Source facility.

Geography: High coastal cliffs and perches in Natlan, with the Flower-Feather Clan's settlement on top. Malinalco Grotto, an underground cavern, lies beneath, reached by the right-hand tunnel at the entrance of the Tenebrous Papilla boss cave. The river valley called Xalac Vale runs from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to the clan's settlement.

Places: The clan's settlement, with its flight trial grounds and bulletin boards; Malinalco Grotto; and the new harbour Mavuika arranged for arrivals from Nod-Krai.

People: Chief Mutota leads the clan. Its best-known member is Chasca, a Qucusaur rider who is one of the six heroes of Natlan. Ifa, a renowned saurian veterinarian, is also of the clan, as is the elder Allpa, who appears in Chasca's story.

Culture: Members bond with Qucusaurs, and the tribe's Qucusaur Riders are chosen by a hard entrance exam: the applicant must be a proficient warrior and must win a qucusaur's trust. Without full control, rider and saurian could be killed. Those who fail are called Wingless and must give up their saurian partners for safety; life is hard for them. Most other tribes' members rarely talk to a lone member of the clan, and if one begins whistling, something is wrong nearby.

History: During the Abyss's nation-wide assault of Chapter V, the Flower-Feather Clan took the largest amount of damage of any tribe (the wiki's history page ties this to the clan's hero being the only one not yet revealed, without citing a source). Chuychu, who had adopted Chasca into human society, died of Abyssal contamination, and Chasca was then acknowledged by her Ancient Name as the last of the six heroes.

Dangers: The boss Tenebrous Papilla is an Abyssal mimic creature in a cave beneath the cliff. Secret Source automata were reported attacking people near the coast in the lead-up to the Nod-Krai Archon Quest prelude.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the clan is at peace, and the cliff doubles as a haven for Nod-Krai refugees and merchants.

The Abyss no longer threatens Natlan, and Chasca is a hero of the six. The harbour's later effect on the tribe is not described beyond its arrival.

120.content: The Flower-Feather Clan (Tlalocan) is one of Natlan's six tribes. Its chief is Mutota. Its warriors form the Qucusaur Riders and its saurian companions are Qucusaurs. It was founded thousands of years ago by Lianca and has taken in orphans, exiles and banished dragons.

121.content:
Realm of the Night Kingdom: The "Realm of the Night Kingdom" is a quest domain in Natlan's Basin of Unnumbered Flames, entered during the Archon Quest "Into Eternal Night". The domain's own description calls it the realm of the dead, where the "River of Concepts" flows, and says Kachina is trapped here, struggling desperately and needing rescue before it is too late.

Trial characters for the domain are Kachina and Mualani. The route is a series of areas: Tepetlisaur and Yumkasaur beasts in abyss-corrupted form, an optional hilichurl camp, more beasts, a group of Thundercraven Rifthound whelps, and finally an Abyss Lector: Fathomless Flames. The way into the Night Kingdom runs through the Remnants of the Secret Source.

Quests: Archon Quest: Into Eternal Night (version 5.0). Rescuing Kachina is the premise given in the domain text; the quest's details are covered by the quest entry, not here.

Status as of 7.1: A quest-only domain; no standing gameplay use after the quest per the wiki's "temporary" navbox. The Night Kingdom itself persists in Natlan lore as of 7.1.

key: Remnants of the Secret Source excavation site
122.content:
Remnants of Tetenanco (also: Remnants of the Secret Source excavation site): The Remnants of Tetenanco are ancient ruins left by the dragons in Atocpan, Natlan. They are thought to be a satellite city destroyed in the war between the dragons and Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon. Locals now call them the Remnants of the Secret Source excavation site.

A warning notice just south of the guard Mposo says the site is temporarily closed to the public because of frequent recent volcanic eruptions. Mposo guards the site.

Geography: A subarea of Atocpan, a cluster of dragon-made ruins now set up as an excavation site.

People: Mposo watches over the site. Excavators and researchers are implied by the site's use, but only Mposo is placed there.

History: The ruins are believed to have been a satellite city of the dragon civilisation, destroyed in the war between the dragons and Xbalanque. The name Tetenanco comes from Nahuatl and means 'at the ramparts', per the wiki's etymology note.

Dangers: Frequent volcanic eruptions, which is why the site is closed.

Quests: A list of Remnants of Tetenanco quests is attached to the location; A Brief History of Rocks is the one used here as the source of its past.

Status as of 7.1: Closed to the public in-world because of eruptions, as of the latest information read (7.1 cutoff).

123.content:
Remnants of the Secret Source: Remnants of the Secret Source is the ruined former home of ancient dragonkind in Natlan's Basin of Unnumbered Flames, and the only path to the Night Kingdom. Influenced by the Abyss, it hides many unforeseen dangers. It is a quest domain entered during the Archon Quest "Echoes of Life".

The route winds through the ruins. The traveller uses the Spiritsconces of Natlan's saurian creatures in turn: a Yumkasaurus to cross Coilgrass Sigils, a Koholasaurus to travel along a Spiritway, and a Tepetlisaurus to cross a Molten Fissure and smash a rock wall, then climbs a solid phlogiston wall to enter the Night Kingdom.

Quests: Archon Quest: Echoes of Life (version 5.0), in which the Traveller is led toward the Night Kingdom; its plot is covered in the quest entry.

Status as of 7.1: A quest domain; the Night Kingdom beyond it is the destination, and as of 7.1 nothing further is added to the domain.

124.comment: Remnants of the Secret Source: Path to the Night Kingdom
124.content: The domain text calls this the sole path to the Night Kingdom and a former home of ancient dragonkind, now reduced to ruins and corrupted by the Abyss.

125.content:
Ruined Armament Workshop: A ruined facility in the Dragons' Residence of the Ancient Sacred Mountain, Natlan. It once made and stored weapons, and the ancient dragons may also have used it for human experimentation.

A Nest Experiment Log beside a huge dragon statue records one such experiment: a human child cast among the vishaps.

Places: The Nest Experiment Log is on the right side of the huge dragon statue.

History: The log's researcher describes the Regent's so-called test subject, a seemingly ordinary human child, being thrown in with the vishaps and expected to be treated as food. The subject showed strength and recovery far beyond an adult human's, took food from the vishaps and then shared the rest with them, a kindness the researcher notes exceeds anything seen in similar human experiments.

Status as of 7.1: Ruined and accessible as of 7.1.

key: Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame
126.comment: Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame
126.content:
Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame: The Ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame are an instance in Tequemecan Valley, Natlan, unlocked during the quest Revelations from the Past. After the quest, one reaches them from the Hall of Parting Vows by descending glowing stairs to Catastrophe's Edge and touching an inscription.

The Sage of the Stolen Flame is the human-world legend of the dragon prince Kukulkan, who stole phlogiston from the dragons and taught it to humans. The wiki page for these ruins is otherwise very short, so this site is best treated as part of the Hall of Parting Vows trial.

Geography: A separate instance below the Hall of Parting Vows, entered by an inscription beyond Catastrophe's Edge.

History: The Sage, called Waxaklahun Ubah Kan in tribal stories, is said to have taught Natlan's first human tribes to use phlogiston and to have left a token of oath for a worthy human and Saurian pair. He appears in tales from the tribal era, Ochkanatlan and even the cataclysm.

Quests: Revelations from the Past is the only quest tied to the site.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible as of 7.1 once the quest has been completed.

127.content:
Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land: The Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land is a point of interest in the Tezcatepetonco Range of Natlan, within the area of the Masters of the Night-Wind. Its viewpoint is called Ceremonial Site Lost in Night's Dim Light.

Biram is listed as chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind and Caholom as high priest, with Cip as a guard and Tlapo as the Iktomisaurus elder; Toltec is also listed. Yolotli is found in the area labelled Chamber of Weaving.

People: The tribe's leadership and some members are found here; their own entries carry their stories.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an accessible location with named residents. No later changes were found.

128.content:
Sanctum of Rainbow Spirits: The Sanctum of Rainbow Spirits is an empty trial ground in Ameyalco Waters, Toyac Springs, Natlan. Tradition says the first sage to learn phlogiston created a place of great purity here, where warriors were taught to wield prismatic flames and flowing light. The sanctum is now abandoned and occupied by scoundrels.

Later the powers taught here were turned into weapons in conflicts between the tribes, and the disheartened Sage of the Stolen Flame withdrew from the world and faded from many tales. The domain description says the sage, in the form of a rainbow spirit, taught the tribes' warriors the language of phlogiston, but once the Pyro Archon (Xbalanque) seized the authority of flame the trials became unnecessary. Drive out the occupiers and the player may take the artifacts stored here.

Status as of 7.1: Permanently accessible in Natlan as of 7.1; no plot events are tied to it.

129.comment: Sanctum of Rainbow Spirits: The Sage of the Stolen Flame and the rainbow trials
129.content: Flavour text: a sage in rainbow-spirit form taught tribal warriors to speak phlogiston's language; the trials fell out of use after Xbalanque took the flame's authority, and the sage vanished from many tales.

130.content:
Scorchwind Trial Grounds (also: Pakpaka Flying School): The Scorchwind Trial Grounds is a training ground in the Tezcatepetonco Range of Natlan, south of the "Masters of the Night-Wind" tribe. It is the base of the Pakpaka Flying School, which teaches flying with Qucusaurs.

The school appears to be run by the Flower-Feather Clan. Signboards advertise gliding challenges to passers-by, and the place has coaches, trainees and assistants.

Places: The grounds are laid out as a course for flight practice. Three challenge signboards invite visitors to try different gliding tests: a timed run through obstacles, a ring-piercing route, and a high-speed dive. A flying school advertisement invites anyone to sign up and earn their wings, noting that flying contests are held every so often and that there is no need to wait for one.

Culture: Flying with Qucusaurs is a skill the school treats as teachable, with levels of challenge and open contests. The name Pakpaka is likely drawn from a word for "wing" in several Philippine languages.

Atmosphere: Open, windy training ground with ringed courses, banners and the sound of practice runs; lively, competitive and slightly boastful.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the grounds remain a working flying school with permanent gliding challenges.

131.comment: Scorchwind Trial Grounds: Pakpaka Flying School
131.content: The Pakpaka Flying School teaches flying with Qucusaurs and is based at the Scorchwind Trial Grounds in the Tezcatepetonco Range, south of the "Masters of the Night-Wind". It appears to be run by the Flower-Feather Clan and holds contests now and then.

132.content:
Sea of Shifting Sentience: A subarea of the Ancient Sacred Mountain in Natlan with large pools of Liquid Phlogiston. The ancient dragons once submerged themselves in them to take in the knowledge and wisdom stored in the primal flame.

The Chinese name means roughly Sea of Divergent Sentience, and the area has a viewpoint description titled Fiery Flowing Sea of Sentience.

Places: The pools are the area's main feature. One of the Iridescent Legacy collectibles (Part IV) is found here.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible as of 7.1.

133.content:
Seven-Colored Statue: The Seven-Colored Statue is a large statue in the Easybreeze Market of Natlan's Easybreeze Holiday Resort. It resembles an octopus spouting seven bubbles.

The map description suggests that covering the statue in colour earns a reward from the resort. It was added in version 5.8.

Places: The statue stands on the streets of the Easybreeze Market. Its seven bubbles can each be painted a different colour, and the octopus has an eye that serves as the target.

Atmosphere: Bright, playful market street, splashes of colour and a whimsical octopus watching shoppers; a holiday feeling.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the statue remains in Easybreeze Market as a permanent paint-throwing attraction.

134.content: An octopus-like statue with seven bubbles in Easybreeze Market, Natlan. Visitors colour the bubbles with paintballs thrown at its eye and receive rewards from the resort.

135.content:
Seven-Hued Ruins: The Seven-Hued Ruins are the underground remains of the Battle of Seven Colors in Natlan's Tezcatepetonco Range. Citlali, following directions from Etchemin, finds the entrance to the ruined battlefield, and the Traveller goes in with her. The domain's text notes that the secrets of the battle turned out to be buried deep beneath the ground.

The quest is the third part of "The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors" in Citlali's Tribal Chronicles chapter "Memories Flowing With Color" (version 5.3). After analysing the mechanisms and leaving a labyrinth, the party must stop Montluson and his group, a Fatui party that includes the Pyro Agent Grudoc, and then capture Montluson.

Quests: Story quest "Seven-Hued Ruins" (5.3), part 3 of "The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors", between "Please, great shaman!" and "The Color of Memory".

Status as of 7.1: A quest-only domain as of 7.1; its walkthrough on the wiki is incomplete.

136.comment: Seven-Hued Ruins: Entering the Battle of Seven Colors ruins
136.content: Citlali found the entrance with Etchemin's help; inside, the Traveller and Citlali explore the labyrinthine ruins, face abyss-corrupted creatures and then Fatui led by Montluson and Grudoc.

137.content:
Skyfire Circlet (also: Nahuatzin's Springboard): The Skyfire Circlet is a ring of islands floating over the mouth of the Great Volcano of Tollan in Natlan, suspended by the power of Phlogiston. It contains the only entrance to the Ancient Sacred Mountain, which is why it is also called Nahuatzin's Springboard.

It is a subarea of Atocpan, the area that holds the Great Volcano and the home of the Collective of Plenty.

Geography: Floating rock islands in a ring above the crater. Features include ancient-variant Everflame Seeds, Gaseous Phlogiston (with Phlogiston currents, wind tunnels and Scorchwind Conflux), geothermal vents, Saurian Indwelling and Secret Source Sentinels. The local specialty is the Quenepa Berry.

History: Iridescent Legacy Part I records the last words of the sovereign ruler Aj Nimalaj Chuq'ab Hun, one of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords. He says Xbalanque's forces have broken through the Skyfire Circlet, calls the human leader a worthy foe, notes that humanity's grasp of Phlogiston is no more refined than the vishaps' yet enough to counter dragon power, and regrets that the traitor handed fire knowledge to another race. He also admits the dragons' civilisation had stagnated and that humans climbed the Sacred Mountain unnoticed.

Quests: The world quest Nahuatzin's Leap (Path to the Flaming Peaks, part 1; version 5.5) sends the Traveler to the top of the Circlet to leap into the crater.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1; no appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found.

138.content: The Skyfire Circlet is the floating ring above the volcano mouth and the only way into the Ancient Sacred Mountain.

139.content:
Speaker's Chamber (also: Speakers' Chamber): The Speaker's Chamber is a watchtower-like building in a corner of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. The Pyro Archon presides over it, and it coordinates the Stadium's affairs and the six major tribes.

By ancient tradition the tribal chiefs gather by the flame there at regular intervals and negotiate openly under the Pyro Archon's watch.

Governance: The Chamber is the meeting place of the chiefs of Natlan's six major tribes. The Pyro Archon, now Mavuika, presides. Business is to be settled without reservation beside the flame.

Status as of 7.1: Active as the Stadium's council hall as of 7.1.

140.content:
Spiritwall Cave: Spiritwall Cave is a point of interest in Toyac Springs, Natlan. It is a closed-off cave where someone left a half-written, half-drawn note describing years spent making wall paintings.

The writer says a rockfall trapped them there, and that they had run out of the phlogiston used for engraving. The note is unsigned.

History: The note, titled Picturesque Records, is a piece of paper well preserved because of the sealed surroundings. Its author asks how many days have passed since the rockfall trapped them. They regret not seeing an ancient excavation site once more, and speak of the wall paintings they were making.

Atmosphere: Quiet, enclosed and dusty, with a creative loneliness: pictures on the stone, a note in a hopeful and wry voice.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cave and its note remain as discovered; nothing further about the artist is revealed in the sources read.

141.content: Picturesque Records is an unsigned note in Spiritwall Cave, Toyac Springs. Its author, trapped by a rockfall, wrote about turning Phlogiston Engraving into free pictures and graffiti and hoped the art would outlast them.

142.content:
Stadium of the Sacred Flame (also: Sacred Flame Arena): The Stadium of the Sacred Flame is the heart of Natlan, a great arena in the Basin of Unnumbered Flames that serves as the nation's main city and the common ground of its six tribes. Above the arena burns the Sacred Flame, the ever-burning fire that holds back the Abyss and links the living world to the Night Kingdom. Here Natlan held the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, its great combat tournament, and the Ode of Resurrection that brought fallen heroes back to life; here too stands the Speaker's Chamber, where the Pyro Archon Mavuika governs. Since the Abyss was defeated (5.3) the Stadium is a place of peace and sport.

Around the arena lie three busy quarters: Chuwen Fair to the north (market stalls and the Adventurers' Guild), the Temple of Pax to the south (research, shops and the Speaker's Chamber) and the Warrior's Rest Area with the Weary Inn, where Pilgrimage contestants eat and sleep for free.

Geography: The Stadium is a subarea of the Basin of Unnumbered Flames in central Natlan. The Sacred Flame rises from an outlet above the arena itself and can be seen from far outside the Stadium. Chuwen Fair runs along the northern side of the stadium, the Temple of Pax along the southern side, and the Warrior's Rest Area and Weary Inn sit on the outskirts of Chuwen Fair. The Speaker's Chamber is a watchtower-like building in one corner of the complex.

Places: - The arena: the tournament ground at the centre, overlooked by the Sacred Flame; ceremonies, speeches and matches take place here.
- Speaker's Chamber: the Pyro Archon's seat of government and council hall.
- Chuwen Fair (north): market and shops, the Adventurers' Guild desk (Katheryne) and the store of the Saurian Relics Association.
- Temple of Pax (south): an outer concourse, a fair inside, and the temple, which handles academic research such as the study of ancient dragon relics.
- Warrior's Rest Area: the Weary Inn, the Contestant Lounge and street food stalls.

Governance: The Speaker's Chamber, presided over by the Pyro Archon, coordinates the affairs of the Stadium and of the six major tribes. Ancient tradition requires the tribal chiefs to gather by its fire at regular intervals and negotiate openly under the Archon's eye. It also appears to act as Natlan's main judicial body. In Natlan the Pyro Archon is a mortal chosen through the Pilgrimage, which tests candidates in battle.

Culture: The Stadium exists for contest: it hosted the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, whose fights produced the Contending Fire that fuels the Flame, and the Ode of Resurrection.

History: Natlanese tradition holds that after Tenoch united the tribes during the cataclysm 500 years ago, the first Pyro Archon laid down the rules still followed at the Stadium. Mavuika placed her life into the Sacred Flame five hundred years ago as part of her plan to save Natlan, and returned to become Pyro Archon again before the Traveler arrived. In 5.0 Kachina's failed Ode exposed the Abyss's interference and Capitano challenged Mavuika in the arena; in 5.1 the Stadium became Natlan's last stronghold against the Abyssal invasion; in 5.3 Mavuika and the Traveler ended the war from the Night Kingdom while Natlan waited around the Flame.

Quests: Much of Archon Quest Chapter V takes place here, together with Mavuika's story quest (Sol Invictus Chapter) and many world quests and commissions.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Natlan is at peace. The Night Warden Wars are over, so the Ode of Resurrection is no longer held and Ancient Name bearers no longer have to compete. Mavuika has turned the Pilgrimage into a purely athletic competition, which opens the possibility of outsiders taking part.

The first Pilgrimage of the new kind was won by Kinich. Mavuika remains Pyro Archon and still governs from the Speaker's Chamber, though after the events in Nod-Krai she gave the Pyro Gnosis, through the Traveler, to Nahida, who used it to burn down the corrupted Irminsul (Song of the Welkin Moon Act X); the Gnosis has been unaccounted for since. In 6.0 the Traveler's Natlanese friends and Mavuika threw a farewell party for them before they sailed with Ineffa for Nod-Krai.

143.comment: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Chuwen Fair
143.content: Chuwen Fair is the market quarter along the northern side of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. It holds food and goods vendors, the Adventurers' Guild desk run by Katheryne, the store of the Saurian Relics Association (manager Siyah) and the paint shop Frida's Palette (owner Acat). On tournament days a courier works the fair, and the Weary Inn lies on its outskirts.

144.comment: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Temple of Pax
144.content: The Temple of Pax occupies the southern side of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame: an outer concourse, an inner fair and the temple itself, which handles academic research, including the study of ancient dragon relics. Vendors include The Salutary Furnace (owner Alom). The Speaker's Chamber belongs to this part of the complex.

145.comment: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Warrior's Rest Area and the Weary Inn
145.content: The Warrior's Rest Area of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame houses the Contestant Lounge (doctor Erinle, manager Karpa), street food at Zakan's Street Bites and the Weary Inn. The Weary Inn is a restaurant and hotel on the outskirts of Chuwen Fair that feeds and houses Pilgrimage contestants and their families for free on the eve of the tournament, at the Pyro Archon's expense. Its name expresses the wish that warriors leave their weariness there and enter the Stadium refreshed. Its managers are said to be chosen by the Speaker's Chamber, and it has become the city's favourite place to celebrate.

146.comment: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Speaker's Chamber
146.content: The Speaker's Chamber is a watchtower-like building in a corner of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. The Pyro Archon presides there over the affairs of the Stadium and the six tribes, whose chiefs traditionally meet around its fire at regular intervals to negotiate openly. It also seems to serve as Natlan's highest court. A fire pit at its centre is itself an outlet of the Sacred Flame. A small display room at the back kept the Pyro Archons' collection of warriors' keepsakes until Mavuika burned them in 5.0 to rescue Kachina.

147.comment: Stadium of the Sacred Flame: Kachina's failed Ode at the Stadium
147.content: After Kachina fell in the Night Warden Wars, an Ode of Resurrection was held for her in the Stadium (Archon Quest Chapter V Act II).
